## Document: 13_pulse_system_visual_scripting_engine.md
# Source 2 Pulse Node Engine & Bytecode Virtual Machine

**Target Subsystem:** Source 2 Pulse Visual Scripting Engine (`pulse_system.dll`)  
**Binaries Analyzed:** `pulse_system.dll`, `server.dll`, `client.dll`  
**Baseline Build Reference:** 15 October 2026 (SteamDB Patch/Build ID: `25966348`)  
**Custom Tooling & Verification:** `simulators/cs2_pulse_vm_sim.cpp`, `simulators/build_pulse_sim.bat`  
**Ghidra Reversal Anchors:** `CPulseCell_Base` VTable (`0x180143dd8`), Instruction Dispatcher (`0x18008f810`), Opcode String Table (`0x13f150`)

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Architecture Overview

In Counter-Strike 2, entity logic, state machines, and scripted behaviors are driven by **Pulse**: a high-performance, asynchronous, graph-compiled bytecode virtual machine hosted inside `pulse_system.dll`.

Pulse powers complex game logic across Source 2:
- **Map & Game Mode Logic:** Objective timers, door sequencing, bomb site boundaries, and scripted encounters.
- **Weapon & Animation State Machines:** AnimGraph event triggers, sound event binding, and particle sequence orchestration.
- **Asynchronous Execution:** Built-in coroutine-style yielding where graph nodes (`CPulseCell_Inflow_Wait`) can sleep for game-time durations or wait for external game events without stalling the tick engine or blocking parallel node executions.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Authoring ["Hammer 2 / Pulse Editor"]
        Editor["Visual Node Graph (.pulse / .vmdl_c)"] --> Compiler["Pulse Graph Compiler"]
    end

    Compiler --> Asset["Compiled CPulseGraphDef Asset<br/>- PGDInstruction_t Bytecode Array<br/>- Constant Pool & Variable Layout<br/>- Execution Chunks"]

    subgraph Runtime ["pulse_system.dll Execution Runtime"]
        Asset --> Instance["CPulseGraphInstance<br/>(Graph Memory & State Variables)"]
        Instance --> RootCursor["Root Pulse Cursor<br/>(Instruction Pointer & Registers)"]

        RootCursor --> Dispatcher["Instruction Dispatcher Loop<br/>(0x18008f810)"]
        Dispatcher --> FastMath["Register Arithmetic / Logic<br/>(ADD_INT, SCALE_VEC3, JUMP)"]
        Dispatcher --> YieldCell["Yielding Cell Execution<br/>(CPulseCell_Inflow_Wait)"]
        Dispatcher --> ForkOutflow["Child Cursor Forking<br/>(OP_CREATE_CHILD_CURSOR_OUTFLOW)"]

        YieldCell -.->|Suspend Cursor| WaitQueue["Instance Sleep Queue<br/>(Wakes on GameTime)"]
        ForkOutflow --> ChildCursor["Child Pulse Cursor<br/>(Independent Chunk Pointer)"]
    end
```

---

## 2. Binary Structure: The 56-Byte `PGDInstruction_t`

Reverse engineering of `pulse_system.dll` in Ghidra revealed that unlike traditional variable-length bytecode streams (such as Lua or Java bytecode), Source 2 Pulse executes **fixed-width 56-byte instruction packets** (`PGDInstruction_t`). This design eliminates instruction alignment parsing overhead, ensures predictable memory stride during cache prefetching, and allows direct direct-mapped jumps.

### 2.1 Binary Layout Specification

```
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                        PGDInstruction_t (56 Bytes)                       |
+---------------------+-------------------+-------------------+------------+
| Offset (Hex)        | Field Name        | Type              | Size       |
+---------------------+-------------------+-------------------+------------+
| 0x00 - 0x01         | m_nCode           | int16_t           | 2 bytes    |
| 0x02 - 0x03         | m_nVar            | int16_t           | 2 bytes    |
| 0x04 - 0x05         | m_nReg0 (Dest)    | int16_t           | 2 bytes    |
| 0x06 - 0x07         | m_nReg1 (Src A)   | int16_t           | 2 bytes    |
| 0x08 - 0x09         | m_nReg2 (Src B)   | int16_t           | 2 bytes    |
| 0x0A - 0x0B         | m_nConstIdx       | int16_t           | 2 bytes    |
| 0x0C - 0x0F         | m_nChunk          | int32_t           | 4 bytes    |
| 0x10 - 0x13         | m_nDestInstruction| int32_t           | 4 bytes    |
| 0x14 - 0x17         | m_nCallTarget     | int32_t           | 4 bytes    |
| 0x18 - 0x1B         | m_nSymbolOffset   | int32_t           | 4 bytes    |
| 0x1C - 0x37         | m_ReservedPadding | uint8_t[28]       | 28 bytes   |
+---------------------+-------------------+-------------------+------------+
Total Size: 56 Bytes (0x38)
```

### 2.2 Register-Based Execution Model

Pulse is an explicit **3-address register machine**:
- `m_nReg0`: Target destination register index (`r0`, `r1`, `r2`, ...).
- `m_nReg1`: Left-hand operand source register.
- `m_nReg2`: Right-hand operand source register.

Registers hold strongly typed `PulseValue` variants supporting `bool`, `int32_t`, `float`, `Vector3D`, `CUtlStringToken`, and `CEntityHandle`.

---

## 3. Complete Instruction Set: The 122 Pulse Opcodes

By analyzing the opcode symbol table at `.rdata:0x13f150` in `pulse_system.dll`, we recovered the entire opcode enum `PulseInstructionCode_t`, spanning indices `0x00` through `0x79` (122 opcodes):

| Opcode ID | Symbolic Mnemonic | Operation Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `0x00` | `IMMEDIATE_HALT` | Terminates the calling execution cursor immediately. |
| `0x01` | `RETURN_VOID` | Returns from chunk subroutine with no return value. |
| `0x02` | `RETURN_VALUE` | Copies register value to parent cursor return slot and halts. |
| `0x03` | `NOP` | No-op padding instruction. |
| `0x04` | `JUMP` | Unconditional jump to `m_nDestInstruction` within current chunk. |
| `0x05` | `JUMP_COND` | Branch to `m_nDestInstruction` if boolean register `m_nReg0` is true. |
| `0x06` | `CHUNK_LEAP` | Transfers cursor execution to target chunk `m_nChunk` at instruction `m_nDestInstruction`. |
| `0x07` | `GET_CONST` | Loads constant pool entry `m_nConstIdx` into destination `m_nReg0`. |
| `0x08` | `GET_VAR` | Reads instance variable `m_nVar` into register `m_nReg0`. |
| `0x09` | `SET_VAR` | Writes register `m_nReg0` into instance variable `m_nVar`. |
| `0x0A` | `COPY_REG` | Copies source register `m_nReg1` to destination `m_nReg0`. |
| `0x0B` | `ADD_INT` | Integer addition: `Reg[0] = Reg[1] + Reg[2]`. |
| `0x0C` | `SUB_INT` | Integer subtraction: `Reg[0] = Reg[1] - Reg[2]`. |
| `0x0D` | `MUL_INT` | Integer multiplication: `Reg[0] = Reg[1] * Reg[2]`. |
| `0x0E` | `DIV_INT` | Integer division: `Reg[0] = Reg[1] / Reg[2]`. |
| `0x0F` | `MOD_INT` | Integer modulus: `Reg[0] = Reg[1] % Reg[2]`. |
| `0x10` | `LT_INT` | Integer comparison: `Reg[0] = (Reg[1] < Reg[2])`. |
| `0x11` | `LTE_INT` | Integer comparison: `Reg[0] = (Reg[1] <= Reg[2])`. |
| `0x12` | `EQ_INT` | Integer equality: `Reg[0] = (Reg[1] == Reg[2])`. |
| `0x13` | `NEQ_INT` | Integer inequality: `Reg[0] = (Reg[1] != Reg[2])`. |
| `0x14` | `ADD_FLOAT` | Floating-point addition: `Reg[0] = Reg[1] + Reg[2]`. |
| `0x15` | `SUB_FLOAT` | Floating-point subtraction: `Reg[0] = Reg[1] - Reg[2]`. |
| `0x16` | `MUL_FLOAT` | Floating-point multiplication: `Reg[0] = Reg[1] * Reg[2]`. |
| `0x17` | `DIV_FLOAT` | Floating-point division: `Reg[0] = Reg[1] / Reg[2]`. |
| `0x18` | `ADD_VEC3` | 3D Vector addition: `Reg[0] = Reg[1] + Reg[2]`. |
| `0x19` | `SUB_VEC3` | 3D Vector subtraction: `Reg[0] = Reg[1] - Reg[2]`. |
| `0x1A` | `SCALE_VEC3` | 3D Vector scaling: `Reg[0] = Reg[1] * Reg[2]` (scalar float). |
| `0x1B` | `DOT_VEC3` | 3D Vector dot product: `Reg[0] = Reg[1] . Reg[2]`. |
| `0x1C` | `CROSS_VEC3` | 3D Vector cross product: `Reg[0] = Reg[1] x Reg[2]`. |
| `0x1D` | `CREATE_CHILD_CURSOR_OUTFLOW` | **Asynchronous fork:** Spawns a new independent cursor executing target chunk `m_nChunk`. |
| `0x1E` | `CELL_INVOKE` | Dispatches virtual cell method (e.g. wait timers, entity queries, raycasts). |
| `...` | `...` | Full math matrix operations through `SCALE_INV_VEC2` (`0x79`). |

---

## 4. Cursor Lifecycle & Asynchronous Execution Model

The core execution unit of Pulse is the **`PulseCursor`**. Unlike an OS thread or a monolithic Lua coroutine:
1. **Parallel Outflows:** A single graph instance can execute dozens of cursors simultaneously. When a node forks (e.g., an explosion triggering a sound, a screen shake, and a damage delay concurrently), `OP_CREATE_CHILD_CURSOR_OUTFLOW` clones register context into a new cursor.
2. **Non-Blocking Sleep:** When a cursor reaches a wait condition (such as `CPulseCell_Inflow_Wait`), it sets `m_bYielded = true` and records `m_flWakeGameTime`. The virtual machine suspends that specific cursor while sibling cursors continue ticking without interruption.
3. **Tick Re-evaluation:** Each engine tick (`CPulseGraphInstance::ExecuteTick`), the VM checks all sleeping cursors against current `m_flCurrentGameTime`. When the wake condition is reached, `m_bYielded` is cleared and execution resumes at the instruction immediately following the yielding cell.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Engine as "Source 2 Tick Engine"
    participant VM as "CPulseGraphInstance"
    participant C0 as "Root Cursor (Chunk 0)"
    participant C1 as "Child Cursor (Chunk 1)"

    Engine->>VM: ExecuteTick(dt = 0.0156s)
    VM->>C0: ExecuteCursor()
    C0->>C0: OP_GET_VAR / OP_ADD_INT (Accumulator)
    C0->>VM: OP_CREATE_CHILD_CURSOR_OUTFLOW (Chunk 1)
    VM->>C1: Spawn Child Cursor
    C0->>C0: OP_IMMEDIATE_HALT (Terminated)
    VM->>C1: Execute initial instructions
    C1->>C1: OP_CELL_INVOKE (Yield for 3.50s)
    Note over C1: m_bYielded = true<br/>WakeTime = 3.5156s

    Engine->>VM: ExecuteTick(dt = 2.0000s, Time = 2.0156s)
    VM->>C1: Check WakeTime (2.0156s < 3.5156s)
    Note over C1: Still sleeping - tick skips C1

    Engine->>VM: ExecuteTick(dt = 1.6000s, Time = 3.6156s)
    VM->>C1: Check WakeTime (3.6156s >= 3.5156s)
    Note over C1: Wake up! m_bYielded = false
    VM->>C1: Resume execution
    C1->>C1: OP_SET_VAR (m_bIsDefused = true)
    C1->>C1: OP_IMMEDIATE_HALT (Terminated)
    Note over VM: All cursors finished (Active = 0)
```

## 5. RTTI, SchemaSystem & Cell VTable Layout

In `pulse_system.dll`, all node types inherit from `CPulseCell_Base`. Through Ghidra vtable inspection at `0x180143dd8`, we mapped the core virtual dispatch table:

```cpp
// VTable @ 0x180143dd8 (CPulseCell_Base)
class CPulseCell_Base {
public:
    virtual ~CPulseCell_Base() = default;                                     // Slot 0
    virtual const char* GetCellName() const = 0;                              // Slot 1
    virtual PulseCursorYieldResult_t Execute(CPulseGraphInstance* pInstance,  // Slot 2
                                             PulseCursor* pCursor) = 0;
    virtual void OnCursorWake(CPulseGraphInstance* pInstance,                 // Slot 3
                              PulseCursor* pCursor) = 0;
    virtual void OnCursorCanceled(CPulseGraphInstance* pInstance,             // Slot 4
                                  PulseCursor* pCursor) = 0;
    virtual bool ValidateInputs(const CPulseGraphDef* pGraphDef) const = 0;   // Slot 5
};
```

SchemaSystem registration inside `pulse_system.dll` includes 103 classes, forming the core hierarchy:
- `CPulseGraphDef`: Master compiled container holding chunks, constants, and variable declarations.
- `CPulse_Chunk`: Contiguous vector of `PGDInstruction_t` packets.
- `CPulse_Variable`: Named runtime state variable with observable change notification flags.
- `CPulse_RegisterInfo`: Register type map for verification before execution.
- `CPulseCell_Inflow_Base`: Base for execution entry points (events, triggers, wait callbacks).
- `CPulseCell_Outflow`: Output pin trigger node initiating subsequent chunks.

## 7. Strategic Impact for Source 2 Reverse Engineering & Tooling

Understanding `pulse_system.dll` completes a crucial piece of the Counter-Strike 2 engine puzzle:
- **Map & Gamemode Decompilation:** Custom maps compiled with Hammer 2 store their logic in Pulse assets rather than plaintext entity keyvalues. Tools can now disassemble `.vmdl_c` and `.vrman_c` bytecode into readable graph structures.
- **Server Plugin Emulation:** Server frameworks (such as AlliedModders Source2 SDK or Swiftly) can intercept `CPulseCell_Base::Execute` or read/write Pulse instance variables directly in memory.
- **Telemetry & Anti-Cheat Analysis:** Valve's automated server instrumentation binds directly to Pulse observable variables to track bomb plant timestamps, player positioning, and round state transitions.

## 1. Architectural Overview: Authoritative Ballistics & Penetration Pipeline

In Counter-Strike 2, all bullet trajectories, damage evaluation, hitbox detection, and surface wallbang calculations are executed authoritatively on the server (`server.dll`). The client predicts weapon firing animations and client-side impact effects, but bullet penetration and damage attribution are strictly evaluated by `server.dll` using Rubikon physical surface definitions from `vphysics2.dll`.

## 2. authoritatively Reversed Pipeline Routines

### 2.1 Authoritative Firing Dispatcher (`CCSPlayerPawn::FireBullet` @ `0x1802975d0`)
When a player pawn fires a weapon:
1. Validates pawn active weapon (`m_pClippingWeapon`) and extracts weapon economic data (`CCSWeaponData`).
2. Extracts ballistics attributes: `m_flDamage` (base damage), `m_flRange` (maximum ray distance, default 8192 units), `m_flRangeModifier` (distance falloff coefficient), `m_flPenetration` (penetration power), and `m_nNumBullets` (pellet count for shotguns).
3. Evaluates view angles, weapon inaccuracy, and recoil punch to compute the perturbed forward trajectory vector.
4. Enters the per-pellet trace loop calling the internal dispatcher `FUN_180a70240`.

### 2.2 Rubikon Physics Multi-Interval Raycast (`TraceLineIntervals` @ `0x180c26c40`)
Rather than legacy Source 1 single-hit `UTIL_TraceLine`, Source 2 uses `CGamePhysicsQueryInterface::TraceLineIntervals`.
- Rays step through the world geometry, partitioning the trajectory into alternating segments of **Air Intervals** (`flags & 1 == 0`) and **Solid Material Intervals** (`flags & 1 == 1`).
- Each solid segment captures entry coordinate, exit coordinate, surface normals, and material identifiers.

### 2.3 Authoritative Player Capsule Clipping (`ClipTraceToPlayers` @ `0x180181cd0`)
Before solid materials are evaluated, candidate players along the ray are clipped:
1. **Broadphase**: Player world bounds (`mins` to `maxs`) are expanded by a standard `40.0f` unit skin margin.
2. **Narrowphase**: Rays are tested against each active hitbox capsule/OBB from the player's lag-compensated bone hierarchy.
3. If an enemy pawn is intercepted, a hit interval with material `CHAR_TEX_FLESH` (`'F'`) is inserted at the exact hit fraction.

## 4. Mathematical Penetration & Damage Formulations

The core penetration calculation loop is decompiled from `FUN_180a8fca0` in `server.dll`:

### 4.1 Damage Distance Falloff Formula
For bullet travel through air intervals (`flags & 1 == 0`):

$$\text{Damage}_{\text{remaining}} = \text{Damage}_{\text{base}} \times (\text{RangeModifier})^{\frac{\text{Distance}}{500.0}}$$

```cpp
// Reversed assembly @ 0x180a8fd0a:
// DIVSS XMM7, dword ptr [0x18178c014]   ; / 500.0f
// CALL powf                             ; pow(rangeModifier, distance / 500.0f)
// MULSS XMM0, XMM6                      ; * currentDamage
float ApplyDistanceFalloff(float baseDamage, float rangeModifier, float distance) {
    return baseDamage * std::pow(rangeModifier, distance / 500.0f);
}
```

### 4.2 Solid Surface Damage Absorption Formula
When penetrating a solid material:
1. **Thickness Calculation**:
   $$\text{Thickness} = \|\mathbf{v}_{\text{Exit}} - \mathbf{v}_{\text{Enter}}\|$$
2. **Penetration Modifier Inversion**:
   $$\text{penModInv} = \max\left(0.0, \frac{1.0}{\text{penMod}}\right)$$
3. **Distance Absorption Loss**:
   $$\text{Lost}_{\text{distance}} = \frac{\text{Thickness}^2 \times \text{penModInv}}{24.0}$$
4. **Entry/Exit Shock Absorption Loss**:
   $$\text{Lost}_{\text{entry}} = \max\left(0.0, \frac{3.0}{\text{penPower}} \times 1.25\right) \times (\text{penModInv} \times 3.0) + (\text{damageModifier} \times \text{Damage}_{\text{current}})$$
5. **Total Damage Lost**:
   $$\text{Damage}_{\text{new}} = \text{Damage}_{\text{current}} - (\text{Lost}_{\text{distance}} + \text{Lost}_{\text{entry}})$$

### 4.3 Material Specific Overrides & Coefficients

Reversed from assembly branch discriminators at `0x180a9028a - 0x180a90328`:

- **Same-Material Transitions** (`enterMaterial == exitMaterial`):
  - **Wood (`'W'`) & Cardboard (`'U'`)**: `penMod = 3.0f`
  - **Light Metal / Plastic (`'L'`)**: `penMod = 2.0f`
  - **Thin Surfaces** (`thickness < 6.0` units):
    - **Glass (`'G'`) & Shatterglass (`'Y'`)**: `penMod = 3.0f`, `damageModifier = 0.05f` (minimal damage drop)
    - **Chainlink Fence / Wire Mesh** (Bit 13 set on both faces): `penMod = 32.0f`, `damageModifier = 0.00001f` (virtually zero loss)
  - **Thick Surfaces** (`thickness >= 6.0` units):
    - **Chainlink / Grate**: `penMod = 3.0f`
- **Composite / Heterogeneous Materials** (`enterMaterial != exitMaterial`):
  - `penMod = min(enter.penMod, exit.penMod)`
  - `damageModifier = 0.16f` (standard absorption coefficient @ `0x1819196c8`)

### 4.4 Penetration Failure & Termination Conditions
A bullet stops penetrating (`bullet.stopped = true`) when:
1. Total bullet distance traveled exceeds `3000.0f` units.
2. Effective surface penetration modifier is below `0.10f` (`penMod < 0.1f`).
3. Remaining penetration count drops below 1 (`penetrationCount < 1`).
4. Remaining damage drops below `1.0f` (`currentDamage < 1.0f`).
5. Penetrating a teammate's flesh hitbox when `ff_damage_bullet_penetration` is disabled (`0`).

## 2. Binary `.nav` File Format Specification

The Source 2 navigation mesh format preserves backward compatibility with Source 1 while introducing arbitrary polygon mesh geometry and embedded KeyValues3 metadata tables.

### 2.1 File Header & Metadata
| Offset | Data Type | Field Name | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x00` | `uint32_t` | `m_magic` | Magic header identifier: `0xFEEDFACE` |
| `0x04` | `uint32_t` | `m_version` | Navmesh version number (`1` to `36`) |
| `0x08` | `uint32_t` | `m_subVersion` | Sub-version for extended schema features (present if `version > 9`) |
| `0x0C` | `uint32_t` | `m_bspSize` | Matching `.vpk` / `.bsp` map byte size for validation (present if `version >= 4`) |
| `0x10` | `uint8_t` | `m_isAnalyzed` | Analysis completion status bit (present if `version >= 14`) |

### 2.2 Place Names Directory
If `m_version >= 5`, the file encodes a directory of place strings (`uint16_t count`, followed by `uint16_t length` and ASCII characters per place). Areas reference these names via a 16-bit place index.

### 2.3 Navigation Areas (`CNavArea`)
The file encodes an array of convex navigational polygons:
1. **Area Identifier**: `uint32_t m_id`.
2. **Area Flags**: `uint32_t m_flags` (encoded as 8-bit in versions < 9, 16-bit in < 13, and 32-bit in version >= 13).
3. **Geometry Coordinates**:
   - For versions `< 20`: Axis-aligned bounding box (NW corner `Vector3`, SE corner `Vector3`, `float m_neZ`, `float m_swZ`).
   - For versions `>= 20`: Arbitrary convex polygon vertex count followed by `Vector3` coordinate tuples.
4. **Outgoing Portal Connections**:
   - 4 cardinal directions (`NORTH=0`, `EAST=1`, `SOUTH=2`, `WEST=3`).
   - For each direction: `uint32_t count`, followed by connected `m_areaId` (and `m_edgeId` in version >= 21).
5. **Tactical Hiding Spots**:
   - `uint8_t count` of `HidingSpot` records (20 bytes each: `uint32_t id`, `Vector3 pos`, `uint8_t flags`).
6. **Ladder Links**:
   - `LADDER_UP=0` and `LADDER_DOWN=1` connected ladder ID lists.

### 2.4 Navigation Ladders (`CNavLadder`)
For versions `>= 6`, vertical ladders are stored in a dedicated array:
- `uint32_t m_id`, `float m_width`, `Vector3 m_top`, `Vector3 m_bottom`, `float m_length`.
- `uint32_t m_dir` (cardinal facing normal: North, East, South, West).
- Connected area pointers: `m_topForwardAreaId`, `m_topLeftAreaId`, `m_topRightAreaId`, `m_topBehindAreaId`, `m_bottomAreaId`, `m_bottomLeftAreaId`, `m_bottomRightAreaId`.

### 2.5 KeyValues3 Extended Metadata Block (Version >= 36)
In CS2 update version `36` (`0x24`), `CNavMesh::Load` aligns the buffer stream to an 8-byte boundary and invokes `LoadKV3` to parse embedded dynamic spatial tags, navigation obstacles, and custom movement boundaries.

## 3. Navmesh Attribute Flags & Capabilities

Extracted directly from `navsystem.dll` disassembly (`GetNearestNav` @ `0x180037470`):

| Flag Mask | Bit Position | Constant Name | Tactical & Engine Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x00000002` | Bit 1 | `NAV_MESH_JUMP` | Area requires jump trajectory execution |
| `0x00000004` | Bit 2 | `NAV_MESH_PRECISE` | Precise positioning required; bot cannot cut corners |
| `0x00000008` | Bit 3 | `NAV_MESH_NO_JUMP` | Inhibits jumping in this area |
| `0x00000010` | Bit 4 | `NAV_MESH_STOP` | Bot must come to a brief complete stop |

| `0x00040000` | Bit 18 | `NAV_MESH_CRAWL` | Bot must crawl (Source 2 prone/low space) |
| `0x00080000` | Bit 19 | `NAV_MESH_FIRST_CUSTOM` | Game-specific custom nav volume markup |

## 4. Reverse-Engineered A* Search Heuristic (`NavAreaBuildPath` @ `0x18003bdf0`)

The core A* search algorithm in `navsystem.dll` computes the shortest viable traversal path between `startArea` and `goalArea`.

### 4.1 Cost Function Equations

The evaluation function for any candidate node $n$ is:
$$f(n) = g(n) + \alpha \cdot h(n)$$

Where:
- $g(n)$: Accumulated ground and ladder traversal cost from the origin to node $n$.
- $\alpha$: Inadmissible heuristic factor controlled by `nav_pathfind_inadmissable_heuristic_factor` (default `1.0f`).
- $h(n)$: 3D Euclidean distance heuristic with vertical climb penalty.

### 4.2 Vertical Elevation Penalty Formula
Decompiled from `0x18003c400` in `navsystem.dll`:
$$dx = x_{\text{goal}} - x_n$$
$$dy = y_{\text{goal}} - y_n$$
$$\Delta z_{\text{raw}} = |z_{\text{goal}} - z_n|$$
$$\Delta z_{\text{clamped}} = \min(\Delta z_{\text{raw}}, 2 \cdot h_{\text{step}}) \quad \text{where } h_{\text{step}} = 18.0 \text{ units}$$
$$\Delta z_{\text{penalized}} = (\Delta z_{\text{raw}} - \Delta z_{\text{clamped}}) \times 3.0 + \Delta z_{\text{clamped}}$$
$$h(n) = \sqrt{dx^2 + dy^2 + (\Delta z_{\text{penalized}})^2}$$

> **Key Takeaway**: Any vertical elevation change exceeding standard step climb clearance ($36.0$ units) incurs a steep **$3.0\times$ penalty** in the heuristic distance, naturally biasing bots toward stairs, ramps, and elevators over high cliff drops or steep mantle points.

### 4.3 Traversal Cost Calculation (`CNavPathCost` @ `0x18003b420`)
1. **Ground Traversal**:
   - Calculates the closest portal point on the shared boundary segment between `currentArea` and `neighborArea`.
   - Computes segment Euclidean distance $d$.
   - Multiplies by area modifiers:
     - $d \times 1.35$ if `NAV_MESH_CROUCH` is set.
     - $d + 50.0$ if `NAV_MESH_JUMP` is set.
     - $d \times 3.0$ if `NAV_MESH_AVOID` is set.
2. **Ladder Traversal**:
   - If `m_bAllowLadders` is false, returns $-1.0f$ (blocking traversal).
   - If allowed, returns $\text{ladder.length} \times 1.5$.

# Counter-Strike 2 (Source 2) - Weapon Inaccuracy, Spread Cone & Recoil Punch Decay Pipeline

> **Binary Targets**: `client.dll` & `server.dll` (Base Address: `0x180000000`)  
> **Key Routines**: `C_CSWeaponBase::GetInaccuracy` (`0x18080c1a0`), `FX_CalculateSpread` (`0x180d23fe0`), `FX_FireBullets` (`0x180d237d0`), `C_CSWeaponBase::UpdateAccuracyPenalty` (`0x180827be0`), `GetRecoveryTime` (`0x18080cef0`), `CalculateStrafingInaccuracy` (`0x18080d4c0`), `UpdateTurningInaccuracy` (`0x180828d90`), `CPlayer_AimPunchServices::SimulateAimPunchDecay` (`0x18085dc60`)  
> **Reconstructed Source**: [`weapon_accuracy.h`](../game/client/weapon_accuracy.h), [`weapon_accuracy.cpp`](../game/client/weapon_accuracy.cpp)  
> **Reference Simulator**: [`cs2_weapon_spread_recoil_sim.cpp`](simulators/cs2_weapon_spread_recoil_sim.cpp), [`build_weapon_spread_sim.bat`](simulators/build_weapon_spread_sim.bat)

## 1. Architectural Overview: Weapon Inaccuracy & Recoil Pipeline

In Counter-Strike 2, shooting accuracy is determined by a layered composite model composed of **intrinsic weapon spread** (`m_flSpread`), **posture and movement inaccuracy** (`m_fAccuracyPenalty`), **strafing inaccuracy** (`sv_strafing_inaccuracy`), **view turning inaccuracy** (`sv_turning_inaccuracy`), and **continuous rapid firing recoil index** (`m_flRecoilIndex`). Simultaneously, camera kick and crosshair displacement are governed by the **aim punch spring-damper ODE system** inside `CPlayer_AimPunchServices`.

When firing, bullet trajectory perturbation is calculated by `FX_CalculateSpread` using **dual uniform disk sampling**: an independent disk for accumulated inaccuracy $(r_1, \theta_1)$ and an independent disk for mechanical weapon spread $(r_2, \theta_2)$, which are summed vectorially on the view projection plane.

```mermaid

        STRAFE["Strafing Inaccuracy: Dot(EyeDir, VelDir)"]
```

## 2. Authoritatively Reversed Routines

### 2.1 Weapon Inaccuracy Evaluator (`C_CSWeaponBase::GetInaccuracy` @ `0x18080c1a0` / `0x18080cfd0`)

`GetInaccuracy` synthesizes all active inaccuracy sources into a composite scalar in the range $[0.0, 1.0]$:

```cpp
float C_CSWeaponBase::GetInaccuracy(float* outSpread, float* outJumpInacc);
```

1. **ConVar Overrides**:
   - If `weapon_accuracy_forcespread > 0.0f`, overrides and returns the forced spread value directly.
   - If `weapon_accuracy_nospread != 0`, returns `0.0f` (perfect laser precision).
2. **Base Penalty**:
   - Starts with `m_fAccuracyPenalty` (`+0x1a18`).
3. **Movement Speed Modulation**:
   - Computes planar horizontal speed $v_{\text{2D}} = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2}$.
   - Remaps speed between a deadzone threshold of $34\%$ max weapon speed ($0.34 \cdot v_{\max}$) and full running penalty at $95\%$ max speed ($0.95 \cdot v_{\max}$):
     $$\text{speedFrac} = \text{clamp}\left(\frac{v_{\text{2D}} - 0.34 \cdot v_{\max}}{0.95 \cdot v_{\max} - 0.34 \cdot v_{\max}}, 0.0, 1.0\right)$$
   - **Crouch Power Curve**: If the pawn is ducking (`pPawn->m_flags & FL_DUCKING`), the movement factor is exponentiated by $0.25$:
     $$\text{speedFrac}_{\text{crouch}} = (\text{speedFrac})^{0.25}$$
   - Adds $\text{speedFrac} \cdot \text{m\_flInaccuracyMove}$ to total inaccuracy.
4. **Airborne / Jumping Inaccuracy**:
   - If the player pawn is not on the ground (`!(pPawn->m_flags & FL_ONGROUND)`):
     - Examines absolute vertical velocity $|v_z|$.
     - If near jump apex ($|v_z| \le 200 \text{ u/s}$), uses `m_flInaccuracyJumpApex` (`+0x7bc`).
     - Otherwise, linearly interpolates up to `m_flInaccuracyJumpInitial` (`+0x7b8`) towards terminal falling speed:
       $$\text{frac} = \text{clamp}\left(\frac{|v_z| - 200.0}{800.0 - 200.0}, 0.0, 1.0\right)$$
       $$\text{jumpInacc} = \text{jumpApex} + \text{frac} \cdot (\text{jumpInitial} - \text{jumpApex})$$
5. **Strafing & Turning Inaccuracies**:
   - Appends orthogonal strafing inaccuracy from `CalculateStrafingInaccuracy` (`FUN_18080d4c0`).
   - Appends view turning angular velocity penalty `m_flTurningInaccuracy` (`+0x1a14`).
6. **Clamping**:
   - Total composite inaccuracy is clamped to $[0.0, 1.0]$.

---

### 2.2 Dual Uniform Disk Spread Evaluator (`FX_CalculateSpread` @ `0x180d23fe0` / `0x180d25630`)

Reverse engineered from `client.dll` (`FUN_180d23fe0`), this function is invoked directly by `FX_FireBullets` on every discharged shot:

```cpp
void FX_CalculateSpread(
    uint16_t itemDefIndex,  // param_1: Weapon Econ Item Definition Index
    int32_t numBullets,     // param_2: Pellets/bullets count (1 for rifles, 8/9 for shotguns)
    int32_t weaponMode,     // param_3: Primary (0) or Secondary (1)
    int32_t randomSeed,     // param_4: Deterministic Subtick PRNG Seed
    float inaccuracy,       // param_5: Output of GetInaccuracy()
    float spread,           // param_6: Intrinsic m_flSpread
    float recoilIndex,      // param_7: Current continuous recoil index
    float* pOutSpreadX,     // param_8: Deflection array X
    float* pOutSpreadY      // param_9: Deflection array Y
);
```

#### Dual Uniform Disk Math Formulation:
Unlike legacy Source 1 models that computed a single composite polar coordinate $(r \cdot (\text{inacc} + \text{spread}), \theta)$, Source 2 samples **two independent uniform disks**:

1. **Inaccuracy Disk (Disk 1)**:
   - Radius variate: $r_1 = \text{RandomFloat}(0.0, 1.0)$
   - Angle variate: $\theta_1 = \text{RandomFloat}(0.0, 2\pi)$
   - **R8 Revolver Secondary (Fan-The-Hammer)**:
     If `itemDefIndex == 64 && weaponMode == 1`:
     $$r_1 \leftarrow 1.0 - r_1^2$$
     This non-linear quadratic inversion pushes bullets outward towards the perimeter of the cone, creating an erratic ring dispersion.
   - **Negev Continuous Spin-Up Laser Convergence**:
     If `itemDefIndex == 28 && recoilIndex < 3.0`:
     Repeats $r_1 \leftarrow r_1^2$ for $i = 3$ down to $\lfloor\text{recoilIndex}\rfloor$, then $r_1 \leftarrow 1.0 - r_1$. Spread collapses from wide wild spray to pinpoint laser accuracy as the barrel spins up past 3 bullets.
   - Radial scaling: $R_{\text{inacc}} = r_1 \cdot \text{inaccuracy}$.

2. **Intrinsic Spread Disk (Disk 2)**:
   - For multi-pellet shotguns with precomputed spread patterns (`FUN_1807cdad0`), looks up fixed table values $(\theta_2, r_2)$ at index $(\text{recoilIndex} \cdot \text{numBullets} + i) \pmod{64}$.
   - For rifles, pistols, and SMGs:
     - Radius variate: $r_2 = \text{RandomFloat}(0.0, 1.0)$
     - Angle variate: $\theta_2 = \text{RandomFloat}(0.0, 2\pi)$
   - Applies the same revolver and negev power curves if applicable.
   - Radial scaling: $R_{\text{spread}} = r_2 \cdot \text{spread}$.

3. **View-Plane Vectorial Summation**:
   $$\Delta X = R_{\text{inacc}} \cdot \cos(\theta_1) + R_{\text{spread}} \cdot \cos(\theta_2)$$
   $$\Delta Y = R_{\text{inacc}} \cdot \sin(\theta_1) + R_{\text{spread}} \cdot \sin(\theta_2)$$

---

### 2.3 Accuracy Penalty Update & Exponential Decay (`UpdateAccuracyPenalty` @ `0x180827be0` / `0x180828a10`)

Executes every engine tick to decay accumulated fire recoil penalties back to resting baseline:

1. **Target Posture Inaccuracy**:
   - **Ladder**: Target is `m_flInaccuracyLadder`.
   - **Airborne**: Target is `m_flInaccuracyStand + m_flInaccuracyJump`.
   - **Player Stacking (Boost)**: If standing atop another player pawn and stack depth $\ge \text{weapon\_accuracy\_stack\_boost\_limit}$, applies `m_flInaccuracyLadder * 2.0f`.
   - **Crouching**: Target is `m_flInaccuracyCrouch`.
   - **Standing**: Target is `m_flInaccuracyStand`.
   - **Reloading**: Adds `m_flInaccuracyReload` (`+0x7c0`) if `m_bInReload` is active.
2. **Exponential Recovery ODE Decay**:
   - If $m\_fAccuracyPenalty \ge \text{target}$:
     $$\text{decayFactor} = \exp\left(-\frac{\ln(10.0)}{\text{recoveryTime}} \cdot \Delta t\right)$$
     $$m\_fAccuracyPenalty \leftarrow \text{target} + (m\_fAccuracyPenalty - \text{target}) \cdot \text{decayFactor}$$
   - Where $\Delta t = 0.015625 \text{ s}$ ($64 \text{ Hz}$ tick interval).
   - $\ln(10) \approx 2.302585$ ensures the penalty decays by one full order of magnitude ($90\%$ reduction) across exactly $\text{recoveryTime}$ seconds.
3. **Rapid Continuous Firing Recoil Index Decay**:
   - When firing stops ($t - t_{\text{last\_shot}} > \text{m\_flCycleTime} + \Delta t$):
     $$\text{recoilDecay} = \exp(-2 \ln(10) \cdot \Delta t)$$
     $$m\_flRecoilIndex \leftarrow m\_flRecoilIndex \cdot \text{recoilDecay}$$
   - Cutoff deadzone: When $m\_flRecoilIndex \le 0.1$, it snaps immediately to zero.

---

### 2.4 Weapon Recovery Time Evaluator (`GetRecoveryTime` @ `0x18080cef0`)

Computes the characteristic time $\tau$ (in seconds) required for inaccuracy to reset:

- **Airborne State**: If the player is airborne, recovery time is quadrupled:
  $$\text{recoveryTime}_{\text{air}} = \text{m\_flRecoveryTimeCrouch} \cdot 4.0$$
- **Ladder State**: Uses `m_flRecoveryTimeStand`.
- **Standing vs Crouching**:
  - Crouched: base is `m_flRecoveryTimeCrouch`, final is `m_flRecoveryTimeCrouchFinal`.
  - Standing: base is `m_flRecoveryTimeStand`, final is `m_flRecoveryTimeStandFinal`.
- **Bullet Count Transition**:
  - If `m_flRecoveryTime...Final != -1.0f`, interpolates linearly between base and final recovery times based on recoil bullet index $i_{\text{bullet}}$ between `m_nRecoveryTransitionStartBullet` and `m_nRecoveryTransitionEndBullet`:
    $$\text{frac} = \text{clamp}\left(\frac{i_{\text{bullet}} - \text{start}}{\text{end} - \text{start}}, 0.0, 1.0\right)$$
    $$\tau = \tau_{\text{base}} + \text{frac} \cdot (\tau_{\text{final}} - \tau_{\text{base}})$$

---

### 2.5 Counter-Strike 2 Strafing Inaccuracy (`CalculateStrafingInaccuracy` @ `0x18080d4c0`)

Counter-Strike 2 introduces explicit strafing inaccuracy penalty when counter-strafing or moving perpendicular to the viewing axis:

```cpp
float CalculateStrafingInaccuracy(const PlayerPawnAccuracyContext& ctx, const AccuracyConVars& cvars);
```

1. Computes normalized movement direction $\vec{v}_{\text{dir}} = \frac{\vec{v}}{\|\vec{v}\|}$.
2. Computes eye view direction unit vector $\vec{f}$ via `AngleVectors`.
3. Dot product $\cos\theta = \vec{f} \cdot \vec{v}_{\text{dir}}$.
4. Orthogonal fraction $\text{perpFrac} = 1.0 - |\cos\theta|$.
   - $\text{perpFrac} = 0.0$ when moving purely forward or backward.
   - $\text{perpFrac} = 1.0$ when moving purely sideways (left/right strafe).
5. Non-linear bias power transformation:
   $$\text{biasedPerp} = (\text{perpFrac})^{\text{sv\_strafing\_inaccuracy\_bias}}$$
6. Velocity scaled output:
   $$\text{inaccuracy}_{\text{strafe}} = \left(\frac{\|\vec{v}\|}{250.0}\right) \cdot \text{biasedPerp} \cdot \text{sv\_strafing\_inaccuracy\_scale}$$

---

### 2.6 Recoil Aim Punch Decay ODE (`CPlayer_AimPunchServices::SimulateAimPunchDecay` @ `0x18085dc60` / `0x18085ea90`)

Recoil kick on the camera view is governed by `CPlayer_AimPunchServices`:
- `m_predictableBaseAngle` (`+0x0050`): Current aim punch angular deflection $(\text{pitch}, \text{yaw}, \text{roll})$.
- `m_predictableBaseAngleVel` (`+0x005c`): Angular velocity of the punch.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Kick Impulse (dt=0)"] --> B["Angle Velocity Omega"]
    B --> C["Exponential Damping: exp(-4.5 * dt)"]
    C --> D["Angle Step: Theta += Omega * dt"]
    D --> E["Deadzone Filter: ||Theta||^2 <= 0.140625"]
    E --> F["Clamping [-89 deg, +89 deg]"]
```

#### Discrete Spring-Damper Integration per Tick:
1. **Velocity Damping**:
   $$\vec{\omega}(t + \Delta t) = \vec{\omega}(t) \cdot \exp(-4.5 \cdot \Delta t)$$
2. **Angular Integration**:
   $$\vec{\theta}(t + \Delta t) = \vec{\theta}(t) + \vec{\omega}(t + \Delta t) \cdot \Delta t$$
3. **Deadzone Cutoff**:
   - If $\|\vec{\theta}\|^2 \le 0.140625 \text{ deg}^2$ (corresponding to $0.375^\circ$ magnitude), angular deflection and velocity snap to exactly $(0, 0, 0)$.
   - Otherwise, scales by $(1.0 - \frac{0.140625}{\|\vec{\theta}\|^2})$.
4. **Pitch Clamping**:
   - View pitch is clamped to $[-89.0^\circ, +89.0^\circ]$.

---

## 3. Spread Cone 3D Ray Generation

Given player eye angles $(\text{pitch}, \text{yaw}, \text{roll})$, compute camera basis vectors $\vec{f}$ (forward), $\vec{r}$ (right), and $\vec{u}$ (up) via `AngleVectors`. The perturbed unit trajectory ray is constructed using the dual uniform disk output $(\Delta X, \Delta Y)$:

$$\vec{d}_{\text{bullet}} = \text{Normalize}\left(\vec{f} + \vec{r} \cdot \Delta X + \vec{u} \cdot \Delta Y\right)$$

# Counter-Strike 2 (Source 2) - Sub-Tick UserCmd Wire Serialization & Unpacking Pipeline

> **Binary Targets**: `client.dll`, `engine2.dll`, `networksystem.dll` (Base Address: `0x180000000`)  
> **Key Routines**: `CSubtickMoveStep::_InternalParse` (`0x1804f4950` / `0x1804f5640`), `CSubtickMoveStep::_InternalSerialize` (`0x1804f4c40` / `0x1804f5930`), `CBaseUserCmdPB::_InternalParse` (`0x1804f5c00` / `0x1804f68f0`), `CBaseUserCmdPB::_InternalSerialize` (`0x1804f63f0` / `0x1804f70e0`), `CSGOUserCmdPB::_InternalParse` (`0x1807b0740` / `0x1807b1830`), `CSGOUserCmdPB::_InternalSerialize` (`0x1807b0be0` / `0x1807b1cd0`), `CSGOInput::CreateMove` (`0x180cfa6b0` / `0x180cfbd10`)  
> **Reconstructed Source**: [`usercmd_wire.h`](../game/client/usercmd_wire.h), [`usercmd_wire.cpp`](../game/client/usercmd_wire.cpp)  
> **Signature Verification**: 100% Unique Verified Matches across version archives (`client.dll` baseline `2026-10-15_25966348` and latest `2026-10-25_26144732`)

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Architectural Overview

In Counter-Strike 2, player inputs are no longer constrained to discrete, quantized 64 Hz or 128 Hz simulation ticks. Instead, Source 2 introduces a **continuous temporal slicing pipeline** where raw hardware events (keyboard switch edges, mouse clicks, and analog view displacements) are timestamped at high-resolution microsecond precision and serialized into Google Protobuf wire messages (`CSubtickMoveStep`, `CBaseUserCmdPB`, and `CSGOUserCmdPB`).

These command streams are packed into client-to-server net message `clc_Move` (`CCLCMsg_Move`, NetMessage ID `0x15` / 21) using `networksystem.dll`'s variable-bit header protocol, transmitted over encrypted `SteamNetworkingSockets` (SDR), and decoded by `server.dll` to perform exact-sub-tick multi-slice physics integration and lag-compensated hit registration.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph ClientHardware ["Client Hardware & OS"]
        OS_KEY["Raw OS KeyPress (+jump, +duck, +attack)"]
        OS_MOUSE["Raw OS Mouse Delta (dx, dy)"]
        TIMER["High-Resolution Monotonic Clock (QPC)"]
    end

    subgraph CSGOInput_Subsystem ["CSGOInput Pipeline (client.dll)"]
        CREATEMOVE["CSGOInput::CreateMove\n(0x180cfa6b0 / 0x180cfbd10)"]
        SUBTICK_ALLOC["CSubtickMoveStep Constructor\n(56-byte 0x38 struct)"]
        SUBTICK_MATH["Fraction Math:\nwhen = clamp((t_event - t_start) / dt, 0.0, 1.0)"]
```

### 3.2 Protobuf Wire Tag Derivation: Repeated Field 18 (`0x92 0x01`)

Protobuf field keys are serialized as:
$$\text{Tag} = (\text{Field Number} \ll 3) \mid \text{Wire Type}$$

For `CBaseUserCmdPB::subtick_moves`:
- **Field Number**: 18
- **Wire Type**: 2 (`LengthDelimited`)
- Tag calculation:
  $$\text{Key} = (18 \ll 3) \mid 2 = 144 \mid 2 = 146 = \text{0x92}$$
- Encoded as a standard 7-bit LEB128 VarInt:
  - Byte 1: $(146 \ \& \ \text{0x7F}) \mid \text{0x80} = \text{0x12} \mid \text{0x80} = \text{0x92}$
  - Byte 2: $146 \gg 7 = 1 = \text{0x01}$
  - Resulting 2-byte wire tag: `0x92 0x01`

Disassembly confirmation from `CBaseUserCmdPB::_InternalParse` (`FUN_1804f5c00` @ `0x1804f617a`):
```c
case 0x12: // 18 in decimal
    if (bVar6 == 0x92) {
        do {
            // Allocate CSubtickMoveStep into RepeatedPtrField
            uVar3 = FUN_1804f74a0(*(undefined8 *)(param_1 + 0x18));
            param_2 = (byte *)FUN_181250d30(param_3, uVar3, param_2 + 2);
        } while ((param_2 < (byte *)*param_3) && (*(short *)param_2 == 0x192)); // Little-endian 0x0192 = bytes {0x92, 0x01}
    }
```

## 4. Sub-Tick Temporal Mathematics

### 4.1 Sub-Tick Fraction Continuous Normalization

When an asynchronous hardware interrupt occurs (mouse packet or keyboard scan code), `CSGOInput::CreateMove` computes the normalized time fraction $w$:

$$w = \text{clamp}\left(\frac{T_{\text{event}} - T_{\text{tick\_start}}}{\Delta t_{\text{tick}}}, 0.0, 1.0\right)$$

Where:
- $T_{\text{event}}$: High-resolution monotonic timestamp of the hardware transition (seconds)
- $T_{\text{tick\_start}}$: Simulation tick anchor timestamp (seconds)
- $\Delta t_{\text{tick}} = \frac{1}{64.0\text{ s}} = 0.015625\text{ s}$ ($15.625\text{ ms}$)

### 4.2 Multi-Slice Movement Physics Integration

In Source 2's movement engine, each $15.625\text{ ms}$ tick is partitioned into temporal slices at every sub-tick event $w$:

1. **Slice 1 (Ground Pre-Transition)** for duration $\Delta t_1 = w \cdot \Delta t$:
   $$\mathbf{v}_1 = \mathbf{v}_0 + \mathbf{a}_{\text{friction}}(\mathbf{v}_0) \cdot \Delta t_1$$
   $$\mathbf{x}_1 = \mathbf{x}_0 + \frac{\mathbf{v}_0 + \mathbf{v}_1}{2} \cdot \Delta t_1$$

2. **Transition Impulse (Instantaneous @ $t = w \cdot \Delta t$)**:
   $$\mathbf{v}_{z,\text{post}} = \mathbf{v}_{z,1} + \text{sv\_jump\_impulse} \quad (\approx 301.993359\text{ units/s})$$
   $$\text{on\_ground} = \text{false}$$

3. **Slice 2 (Air Post-Transition)** for duration $\Delta t_2 = (1.0 - w) \cdot \Delta t$:
   $$\mathbf{v}_2 = \mathbf{v}_{1,\text{post}} + \mathbf{g} \cdot \Delta t_2 \quad (\mathbf{g} = (0, 0, -800)\text{ units/s}^2)$$
   $$\mathbf{x}_2 = \mathbf{x}_1 + \mathbf{v}_{1,\text{post}} \cdot \Delta t_2 + \frac{1}{2}\mathbf{g}(\Delta t_2)^2$$

```
Tick Start (t = 0.0)             Sub-Tick Event (t = w * dt)           Tick End (t = 1.0)
|--------------------------------------------*------------------------------------------|
<--------- Slice 1: Ground Friction --------><--------- Slice 2: Airborne Gravity ------->
                   dt1 = w * dt                                 dt2 = (1 - w) * dt
```

## 5. Network Wire Framing & Transmission Sequence

The transmission sequence from `CSGOInput` to SDR socket transport follows strict variable-bit encoding:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant OS as "OS / Raw Input"
    participant Input as "CSGOInput (client.dll)"
    participant PB as "Protobuf Serialization"
    participant Net as "networksystem.dll"
    participant SDR as "SteamNetworkingSockets"

    OS->>Input: KeyDown (+jump) @ t = 6.25ms (w = 0.40)
    Note over Input: CreateSubtickMoveStep(button=IN_JUMP, pressed=true, when=0.40)
    Input->>PB: CBaseUserCmdPB::add_subtick_moves()
    Input->>PB: CSGOUserCmdPB::_InternalSerialize()
    Note over PB: Writes Base (tag 0x0A), History (tag 0x12), Attack Index
    PB->>Net: CCLCMsg_Move::_InternalSerialize()
    Note over Net: Writes NetMessage ID 0x15 (10-bit Variable-Bit Header)
    Note over Net: Writes LEB128 VarInt32 Byte Length
    Net->>SDR: Zero-Copy Byte Blit to Packet Buffer
    SDR-->>OS: SDR Encrypted UDP Frame Dispatched
```

### 5.1 Variable-Bit Header Layout for `clc_Move` (`0x15` / 21)

From `networksystem.dll` (`FUN_1801bf5c0` / `ReadVariableBitMessageId`):
- For message ID $21 \in [16, 255]$:
  - **Tier Prefix**: `0b01` (4 extra bits $\to$ 10 bits total)
  - **Lower 4 bits**: $21 \ \& \ \text{0x0F} = 5 = \text{0b0101}$
  - **Initial 6 bits**: $(\text{0b01} \ll 4) \mid \text{0b0101} = \text{0b010101} = \text{0x15}$
  - **Upper 4 bits**: $21 \gg 4 = 1 = \text{0b0001}$
  - **Total 10-bit bitstream**: `0b0001010101`

## 1. Architectural Overview: Server-Side Lag Compensation Pipeline

In Counter-Strike 2, all hit registration, raycasting, and hitbox penetration are evaluated authoritatively on the game server (`server.dll`). Because network latency causes every connected client to view other players at delayed spatial coordinates, the server implements **Authoritative Lag Compensation** (`CLagCompensationManager`).

When a client fires a weapon during a tick, their user command (`CUserCmd`) encodes both the discrete attack tick base and an analog sub-tick timing fraction. Before executing raycasts or capsule collision queries, `server.dll` rewinds candidate target pawns back in time to their exact spatial coordinates and skeletal bone poses as perceived by the firing client. Once hitscan evaluation finishes, `CLagCompensationManager::FinishLagCompensation` restores all pawns back to their current server simulation states.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph ClientCmdFlow ["Client UserCmd Transmission"]
        UC["CUserCmd with Sub-Tick Attack Packet"]
        TS["Extract Tick Base + Sub-Tick Fraction"]
    end

    subgraph LagCompPipeline ["CLagCompensationManager Lifecycle"]
        SLC["StartLagCompensation (0x180ed8c00)"]
        CORE["Core Backtrack Dispatcher (0x180ed6f10)"]
        CLAMP["Clamp to sv_maxunlag (200ms)"]
        SNAP["Take Pre-Rewind RestoreSnapshot"]
        BTP["BacktrackPlayer / BacktrackEntity (0x180eced70)"]
        RING["PawnTrackHistory Ring Buffer Lookup"]
        TPCHECK{"Teleport Breaker: Distance >= 64 units?"}
        LERP["Sub-Tick Fractional Bone/Origin Lerp"]
        DISCRETE["Nearest Frame Discrete Snap"]
        APPLY["Apply Backtracked Hitbox Transforms"]
        HITSCAN["Authoritative Hitscan & Penetration (FireBullet)"]
        FLC["FinishLagCompensation (0x180ebf350)"]
        RESTORE["RestoreEntityTo (0x180ed3f10)"]
    end

    UC --> TS
    TS --> SLC
    SLC --> CORE
    CORE --> CLAMP
    CLAMP --> SNAP
    SNAP --> BTP
    BTP --> RING
    RING --> TPCHECK
    TPCHECK -->|"No (Continuous)"| LERP
    TPCHECK -->|"Yes (Teleported)"| DISCRETE
    LERP --> APPLY
    DISCRETE --> APPLY
    APPLY --> HITSCAN
    HITSCAN --> FLC
    FLC --> RESTORE
```

### 2.2 Public Entrypoint (`CLagCompensationManager::StartLagCompensation` @ `0x180ed8c00`)

When a weapon is discharged on the server:
1. Validates that the shooting player pawn and `CUserCmd` are non-null. If null, triggers fatal assertion `CLagCompensationManager::StartLagCompensation with NULL CUserCmd!!!`.
2. Resolves the attacker pawn handle (`handle & 0x7FFF`) via the global entity system `DAT_181f3de78`.
3. Extracts attack sub-tick timing metadata from the command stream.
4. Invokes the virtual execution dispatcher at VTable offset `0x08` (`0x180ed8e80`), which enters `StartLagCompensationInternal` (`0x180ed6f10`).

```cpp
// Reversed assembly from 0x180ed8c00:
// 48 85 D2                TEST RDX, RDX           ; Test CUserCmd pointer
// 0F 84 55 02 00 00       JZ   fatal_null_cmd     ; Jump to fatal error if null
// 8B 8A 98 0C 00 00       MOV  ECX, [RDX + 0xC98] ; Extract target pawn handle
// ...
// FF 50 08                CALL qword ptr [RAX+8]  ; Invoke VTable[1]
```

---

### 2.3 Core Execution Engine (`StartLagCompensationInternal` @ `0x180ed6f10`)

The core execution engine performs authoritative candidate selection and temporal clamping:
1. **Attacker Exclusion**: Loops over all registered pawns in `m_Pawns`, skipping the firing player (`pawn == attackerPawn`).
2. **Temporal Clamping**: Enforces `sv_maxunlag` ($0.200\text{ s}$ / $200\text{ ms}$). If the requested client rewind delta exceeds 200ms, clamps target time and emits logging telemetry:
   `sv: Lag comp - clamping to sv_max_unlag (%.3f), using target time.`
3. **State Preservation**: Copies the present active transformation into `RestoreSnapshot_t`.
4. **Entity Backtrack**: Calls `FUN_180eced70` (`BacktrackPlayer`) to compute the historical interpolated state and overrides active hitbox matrices.

---

### 2.4 State Restoration (`CLagCompensationManager::FinishLagCompensation` @ `0x180ebf350`)

Reconstructed directly from decompiled routine `FUN_180ebf350`:

```cpp
void CLagCompensationManager::FinishLagCompensation() {
    VPROF_BUDGET("FinishLagCompensation", "LagCompensation");
    
    // Check if lag compensation is currently active (offset +0x78 & +0x79)
    if (!this->m_bLagCompensationActive || !this->m_bNeedRestore) {
        return;
    }

    const int pawnCount = this->m_nTrackedPawnCount;
    for (int i = 0; i < pawnCount; ++i) {
        TrackedEntity_t* entry = &this->m_pTrackedPawns[i];
        if (!entry->m_bIsBacktracked) {
            continue;
        }

        // Resolve 32-bit CEntityHandle: Index (handle & 0x7FFF), Serial (handle >> 15)
        uint32_t handle = entry->m_hEntity;
        if (handle == INVALID_EHANDLE) continue;

        CBaseEntity* entity = ResolveEntityHandle(handle);
        if (entity && entry->m_pRestoreRecord) {
            // Restore original physical transforms and bone hierarchy
            RestoreEntityTo(entity, entry->m_pRestoreRecord);
        }
        entry->m_bIsBacktracked = false;
    }

    this->m_bLagCompensationActive = false;
}
```

---

### 2.5 Transform Restoration & Teleportation Breaker (`RestoreEntityTo` @ `0x180ed3f10`)

`RestoreEntityTo` inspects the record flags bitmask and applies selective state restoration:

1. **Collision Bounding Box** (`flags & 0x08`): Restores `mins` and `maxs` bounds.
2. **Rotation / Eye Angles** (`flags & 0x04`): Restores Euler view angles.
3. **Spatial Origin & Teleportation Breaker** (`flags & 0x02`):
   Computes displacement from the pre-teleport reference origin:
   $$(\Delta x)^2 + (\Delta y)^2 + (\Delta z)^2 < 4096.0\text{ units}^2$$
   If the displacement exceeds $4096.0\text{ units}^2$ ($64.0\text{ units}$), origin restoration is bypassed to prevent teleport snapping glitches.
4. **Skeletal Hierarchy** (`flags & 0x10`): Restores cached 3x4 affine bone transforms (`MAX_BONES = 128`) on the pawn's `CSkeletonInstance`.

---

## 3. Mathematical Rewind & Sub-Tick Interpolation Mechanics

### 3.1 Sub-Tick Timestamp Formula

In Counter-Strike 2, user commands do not operate solely on integer tick numbers. Attack timestamps are continuous analog values derived from the tick interval:

$$t_{\text{subtick}} = \left(\text{tick} + f_{\text{subtick}}\right) \times \Delta t_{\text{interval}}$$

where:
- $\text{tick}$: Discrete command execution tick.
- $f_{\text{subtick}} \in [0.0, 1.0)$: Normalized fractional offset within the tick.
- $\Delta t_{\text{interval}} = \frac{1.0}{64.0} = 0.015625\text{ s}$ ($64\text{ Hz}$ simulation rate).

---

### 3.2 Client Interpolation Rewind Delay

Clients render remote entities using interpolation delay ($t_{\text{interp}}$) defined by `cl_interp_ratio` and packet delivery rate:

$$t_{\text{interp}} = \max\left(\frac{\text{cl\_interp\_ratio}}{\text{cl\_updaterate}}, \Delta t_{\text{interval}}\right)$$

$$t_{\text{target}} = t_{\text{attack}} - t_{\text{interp}}$$

---

### 3.3 Authoritative Unlag Window Clamping (`sv_maxunlag`)

To prevent clients with artificial latency from rewinding players excessively into the past, the server strictly clamps the rewind window:

$$t_{\text{clamped}} = \max\left(t_{\text{cur}} - \text{sv\_maxunlag}, \min\left(t_{\text{cur}}, t_{\text{target}}\right)\right)$$

where $\text{sv\_maxunlag} = 0.200\text{ s}$ ($200\text{ ms}$).

---

### 3.4 Teleport Discontinuity Breaker Condition

Decompiled from `FUN_180ed3f10` (line 72):

$$\|\mathbf{p}_{\text{newer}} - \mathbf{p}_{\text{older}}\|^2 \ge 4096.0\text{ units}^2 \iff \|\Delta \mathbf{p}\| \ge 64.0\text{ units}$$

If a player travels $64.0\text{ units}$ or more between consecutive simulation ticks (e.g. respawn, teleport trigger, spectator toggle), lag compensation marks the track as discontinuous and disables fractional interpolation across that interval.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph ContinuousTrack ["Continuous Motion Track"]
        R1["Record T-1 (0, 0, 0)"] -->|"dist = 4.2u (< 64u)"| R2["Record T (4.2, 0, 0)"]
        R2 -->|"Lerp Fraction = 0.45"| INT["Interpolated Hitbox (1.89, 0, 0)"]
    end

    subgraph DiscontinuousTrack ["Teleport Discontinuity"]
        T1["Record T-1 (100, 200, 0)"] -->|"dist = 1500u (>= 64u)"| T2["Record T (1600, 200, 0)"]
        T2 -->|"Breaker Triggered"| SNAP["Discrete Snap to Nearest Frame"]
    end
```

## 4. Data Structures & Ring Buffer Architecture

### 4.1 3x4 Affine Bone Matrix (`Matrix3x4`)

Source 2 hitboxes are defined relative to bone coordinate spaces represented as 3x4 row-major transformation matrices (3 rows, 4 columns: 3x3 rotation/scale + 3x1 translation):

$$\mathbf{M} = \begin{bmatrix} m_{00} & m_{01} & m_{02} & t_x \\ m_{10} & m_{11} & m_{12} & t_y \\ m_{20} & m_{21} & m_{22} & t_z \end{bmatrix}$$

Linear interpolation between two bone poses at fraction $f \in [0.0, 1.0]$:

$$\mathbf{M}_{\text{interp}} = \mathbf{M}_{\text{older}} + \left(\mathbf{M}_{\text{newer}} - \mathbf{M}_{\text{older}}\right) \times f$$

---

### 4.2 History Record Structure (`LagRecord_t`)

```cpp
struct LagRecord_t {
    uint32_t tickCount;                              // Server simulation tick index
    float simulationTime;                         // Authoritative timestamp (seconds)
    float subTickFraction;                        // Continuous analog sub-tick offset [0.0, 1.0)
    Vector3 origin;                               // World-space pawn origin coordinates
    QAngle eyeAngles;                             // Eye/head orientation angles
    Vector3 mins;                                 // Collision bounding box minimum
    Vector3 maxs;                                 // Collision bounding box maximum
    std::array<Matrix3x4, MAX_BONES> boneMatrices;// Resolved world-space bone transforms
    size_t boneCount;                             // Active bone count (<= 128)
    uint8_t flags;                                // Transform modification bitflags
    Vector3 preTeleportOrigin;                    // Reference origin for 4096.0 sqr distance check
};
```

## Document: 19_hit_registration_and_armor_damage.md
# 19. Hit Registration, HitGroup Multipliers & Kevlar/Helmet Damage Formulas

> **Target Binary:** `server.dll` (Baseline Build `25966348` $\to$ Latest Build `26144732`)  
> **Reconstructed SDK:** [`game/server/hit_registration_damage.h`](../game/server/hit_registration_damage.h) | [`game/server/hit_registration_damage.cpp`](../game/server/hit_registration_damage.cpp)

---

## 1. Executive Summary

When a server-authoritative raycast (`FX_FireBullets` $\to$ `EvaluateBulletPenetration`) intersects a lag-compensated player hitbox capsule (`CGameTrace::m_nHitGroup`), `server.dll` constructs a `CTakeDamageInfo` payload and dispatches it through `CCSPlayerPawn::TraceAttack` and `CCSPlayerPawn::OnTakeDamage_Alive`.

Static disassembly of `server.dll` reveals that Counter-Strike 2 evaluates combat damage in four deterministic stages:
1. **Exponential Distance Falloff**: Attenuates base weapon damage per 500 Hammer units of flight distance.
2. **Anatomical HitGroup Scaling**: Multiplies damage by anatomical zone (`4.0x` Head, `1.25x` Stomach, `1.0x` Chest/Arms, `0.75x` Legs) and team-specific `mp_damage_scale_*` ConVars.
3. **Coverage Verification (`CCSPlayerPawn::IsArmored`)**: Inspects `m_ArmorValue` and `m_pItemServices->m_bHasHelmet` against an 8-way jump table indexed by `HitGroup_t`.
4. **Kevlar Absorption & Durability Overflow (`CCSPlayerPawn::ApplyArmorDamageCalculation`)**: Scales damage by $\text{m\_flArmorRatio} \times 0.5$, deducts durability using $\text{flArmorBonus} = 0.5$, handles armor depletion overflow, and truncates final damage to `int32_t`.

---

## 2. Reversed Function Inventory & Canonical Signatures

| Symbol / Routine | Binary | Baseline RVA (`25966348`) | Latest RVA (`26144732`) | Latest VA (`26144732`) | Shift Delta | Role |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CCSPlayerPawn::ApplyArmorDamageCalculation` | `server.dll` | `0x00a81050` | `0x00a8e500` | `0x180a8e500` | `+0xd4b0` | Kevlar/Helmet damage reduction & durability depletion |
| `CCSPlayerPawn::IsArmored` | `server.dll` | `0x00aca700` | `0x00ad7ba0` | `0x180ad7ba0` | `+0xd4a0` | 8-entry jump table verifying Kevlar & Helmet coverage per `HitGroup_t` |

---

## 3. End-to-End Damage Evaluation Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Bullet Ray Hits Lag-Compensated Hitbox Capsule"] --> B["Distance Decay: D_dist = D_base * (RangeMod ^ (d / 500.0))"]
    B --> C["HitGroup Scaling: D_scaled = D_dist * HitGroupMult * TeamScale"]
    C --> D{"CCSPlayerPawn::IsArmored(hitGroup)<br/>(RVA 0x00aca700)"}
    D -->|"False (Legs or Unhelmeted Head)"| H["Final Health Loss = int(D_scaled)"]
    D -->|"True (Kevlar / Helmet Covers Zone)"| E["Mitigated Damage:<br/>D_new = D_scaled * (m_flArmorRatio * 0.5)"]
    E --> F["Armor Durability Cost:<br/>D_armor = max(1.0, (D_scaled - D_new) * 0.5)"]
    F --> G{"D_armor > m_ArmorValue?"}
    G -->|"Yes (Armor Breaks)"| G1["D_armor = m_ArmorValue<br/>D_new = D_scaled - (D_armor / 0.5)"]
    G -->|"No"| G2["Deduct int(D_armor) from m_ArmorValue"]
    G1 --> H
    G2 --> H
    H --> I["m_iHealth = max(0, m_iHealth - int(D_new))"]
```

---

## 4. Stage-by-Stage Mathematical Formulation

### 4.1 Exponential Distance Falloff
Before reaching `TraceAttack`, the bullet simulation loop attenuates the weapon's `m_flDamage` over the ray's traveled distance $d$ (in Hammer units, where $1\text{ unit} \approx 1.905\text{ cm}$):

$$D_{\text{dist}}(d) = D_{\text{base}} \cdot \left(\text{m\_flRangeModifier}\right)^{\frac{d}{500.0}}$$

For example, the AK-47 ($D_{\text{base}} = 36.0$, $\text{m\_flRangeModifier} = 0.98$) loses $2\%$ of its kinetic damage every $500\text{ units}$ ($9.525\text{ meters}$).

---

### 4.2 HitGroup Multipliers & ConVar Modulators
In `server.dll`, each `HitGroup_t` applies a fixed anatomical damage multiplier combined with team-specific scaling ConVars (`mp_damage_scale_ct_head`, `mp_damage_scale_t_head`, `mp_damage_scale_ct_body`, `mp_damage_scale_t_body`):

| `HitGroup_t` ID | Constant Name | Base Multiplier | Kevlar Covered? | Helmet Required? | Notes |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| `1` | `HITGROUP_HEAD` | **$4.00\times$** | Yes | **Yes** (`+0x41`) | Instant kill for AK-47 ($36 \times 4 \times 0.775 = 111\text{ HP}$) |
| `2` | `HITGROUP_CHEST` | **$1.00\times$** | Yes | No | Upper torso & clavicles |
| `3` | `HITGROUP_STOMACH` | **$1.25\times$** | Yes | No | Pelvis & lower abdomen ($+25\%$ bonus damage) |
| `4`, `5` | `HITGROUP_LEFTARM` / `RIGHTARM` | **$1.00\times$** | Yes | No | Upper arms, forearms, and hands |
| `6`, `7` | `HITGROUP_LEFTLEG` / `RIGHTLEG` | **$0.75\times$** | **Never** | N/A | Thighs, calves, and feet bypass Kevlar completely |

---

### 4.3 Coverage Verification (`CCSPlayerPawn::IsArmored` @ `0x00aca700`)

Disassembly of `FUN_180aca700` (shifted to `0x00ad7ba0` in build `26144732` when `m_ArmorValue` moved from `+0x150C` to `+0x1514`):

```nasm
; bool CCSPlayerPawn::IsArmored(CCSPlayerPawn* rcx, int edx_hitgroup)
180aca700: 45 32 C0                   xor     r8b, r8b
180aca703: 83 B9 0C 15 00 00 00       cmp     dword ptr [rcx + 150Ch], 0 ; this->m_ArmorValue <= 0
180aca70a: 7E 3C                      jle     short loc_ret_false
180aca70c: 83 FA 08                   cmp     edx, 8                     ; hitGroup > HITGROUP_NECK
180aca70f: 77 37                      ja      short loc_ret_false
180aca711: 48 63 C2                   movsxd  rax, edx
180aca714: 4C 8D 0D E5 58 53 FF       lea     r9, [ __ImageBase ]
180aca71b: 41 8B 94 81 50 A7 AC 00    mov     edx, [r9 + rax*4 + 0ACA750h]
180aca723: 49 03 D1                   add     rdx, r9
180aca726: FF E2                      jmp     rdx                        ; Switch jump table
```

- **Cases 0, 2, 3, 4, 5 (`GENERIC`, `CHEST`, `STOMACH`, `LEFTARM`, `RIGHTARM`)**: Immediately set `r8b = 1` and return `true`.
- **Cases 1, 8 (`HEAD`, `NECK`)**: Dereferences `this->m_pItemServices` (`[rcx + 0xB18]`) and reads `bool m_bHasHelmet` at offset `+0x41`.
- **Cases 6, 7 (`LEFTLEG`, `RIGHTLEG`)**: Jump to `loc_ret_false` (`return false`).

---

### 4.4 Kevlar Absorption & Durability Depletion (`0x00a81050`)

Inside `CCSPlayerPawn::ApplyArmorDamageCalculation` (`RVA 0x00a81050`, shifted to `0x00a8e500` in build `26144732`), when `IsArmored(hitGroup)` returns `true`:

1. **Effective Armor Penetration**:
   Each weapon defines `m_flArmorRatio` in its VData (typically in the $[1.0, 2.0]$ scale, e.g., $1.55$ for AK-47, $1.40$ for M4A4/M4A1-S, $0.94$ for Glock-18). The engine multiplies this by `0.5f` (`RVA 0x00a810e7`):
   $$r_{\text{eff}} = \text{m\_flArmorRatio} \times 0.5$$
   $$D_{\text{new}} = D_{\text{scaled}} \cdot r_{\text{eff}}$$

2. **Armor Durability Cost**:
   With $\text{flArmorBonus} = 0.5$, every $1\text{ point}$ of Kevlar durability absorbs $2\text{ points}$ of raw blocked damage:
   $$D_{\text{armor}} = \max\left(1.0,\ (D_{\text{scaled}} - D_{\text{new}}) \times 0.5\right)$$

3. **Depletion Overflow Condition**:
   If $D_{\text{armor}} > \text{m\_ArmorValue}$ (e.g., player only has 3 armor points remaining), the remaining armor is consumed and the unabsorbed remainder spills directly into health:

   $$D_{\text{new}} = D_{\text{scaled}} - \frac{\text{m\_ArmorValue}}{0.5}$$

   $$\text{m\_ArmorValue} \leftarrow 0$$

# Valve Source 2 Reconstructed SDK Architecture & C++20 Header Suite

## Executive Summary

To support reverse engineering, simulation testing, and modding on Counter-Strike 2, we authoritatively reversed and reconstructed a production-ready, compilable **C++20 SDK** directly from the synchronized x64 PE binaries (`2026-10-25_26144732`).

The resulting SDK header suite resides under `sdk/` and enforces strict memory-safety and layout guarantees:
- **`sdk/interfaces_registry.hpp`**: Multi-binary `CreateInterface` registry linked list walk, engine clients, cvar managers, memory allocators, and subsystem interface definitions with verified virtual method table RVAs.
- **`sdk/schema_system.hpp`**: Authoritative runtime reflection structures (`CSchemaType`, `SchemaClassFieldData_t`, `CSchemaClassInfo`, `CSchemaSystemTypeScope`) with compile-time MurmurHash2 routines.
- **`sdk/entity_system.hpp`**: 2D entity chunk page-table architecture (`m_EntityChunks`), `0x70`-byte `CEntityIdentity` layout, `CEntityHandle` 15-bit index / 17-bit serial bitfields, and local player resolvers.
- **`sdk/client_classes.hpp`**: Fully resolved client-side class layouts (`C_BaseEntity`, `C_BaseModelEntity`, `CCSPlayerController`, `C_CSPlayerPawn`, `CSkeletonInstance`, `CModelState`, weapon/item/observer services, `C_PlantedC4`) with zero unverified `void*` placeholders.

All headers are compiled cleanly with **MSVC v19.51+ (`/std:c++20 /EHsc /W4 /WX`)** and validated via `static_assert(sizeof(...) == ...)` and `static_assert(offsetof(...) == ...)`.

## 1. Phase 0: Multi-Binary `CreateInterface` Registry Walk

### 1.1 Linked List Topology (`InterfaceReg`)
Every Source 2 engine module exports `CreateInterface(const char* pName, int* pReturnCode)`. The export walks an internal singly-linked list of `InterfaceReg` nodes:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Head["s_pInterfaceRegs (BSS)"] --> Node1["InterfaceReg Node 1\nm_pName: 'Source2EngineToClient001'\nm_CreateFn: 0x78ab0"]
    Node1 --> Node2["InterfaceReg Node 2\nm_pName: 'NetworkClientService_001'\nm_CreateFn: 0x1bf4b0"]
    Node2 --> Node3["InterfaceReg Node 3\nm_pName: 'GameResourceServiceClientV001'\nm_CreateFn: 0x1ab6e0"]
    Node3 --> NodeN["... -> nullptr"]
```

```cpp
using InstantiateInterfaceFn = void* (*)();

struct InterfaceReg {
    InstantiateInterfaceFn m_CreateFn; // +0x00: Function returning interface pointer
    const char*            m_pName;    // +0x08: Null-terminated interface token string
    InterfaceReg*          m_pNext;    // +0x10: Next registry node in DLL
};
static_assert(sizeof(InterfaceReg) == 0x18);
```

## 2. Phase 1: Runtime SchemaSystem (`schemasystem.dll`)

### 2.1 Virtual Methods & MurmurHash2 Lookups
`ISchemaSystem` allows runtime query of any class or member descriptor registered by loaded DLLs:
- **`ISchemaSystem::FindTypeScopeForModule`**:
  - Slot 13 (RVA `0x11350`): Resolves module type scope by ASCII name string (`"client.dll"`).
  - Slot 14 (RVA `0x11510`): Overloaded query accepting pre-hashed scope identifiers.
- **`CSchemaSystemTypeScope::FindDeclaredClass`**:
  - Slot 2 (RVA `0x162B0`): Indirect resolution storing into `CSchemaClassBinding`.
  - Slot 24 (RVA `0x10460`): Hash lookup in scope table (`this + 0x560`).
  - Slot 25 (RVA `0x10380`): Computes 32-bit MurmurHash2 (`seed = len ^ 0xbaadfeed`, `m = 0x5bd1e995`) and calls Slot 24.

### 2.2 Reconstructed Schema Layouts

## 3. Phase 1: Client Entity System Architecture (`client.dll`)

### 3.1 2D Chunk Page-Table Resolution Arithmetic
Source 2 manages up to 32,768 entities (`0x8000`) without contiguous monolithic array reallocations by maintaining a two-level chunked page table at `CGameEntitySystem + 0x10`:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Handle["CEntityHandle (32-bit)\nIndex: handle & 0x7FFF\nSerial: handle >> 15"]
    Handle --> Split{"Index Splitting"}
    Split -->|"chunk = index >> 9 (0..63)"| ChunkIdx["m_EntityChunks[chunk] (+0x10)"]
    Split -->|"slot = index & 0x1FF (0..511)"| SlotIdx["Slot inside Chunk"]
    ChunkIdx --> ChunkBuf["Contiguous Chunk Buffer\n512 x 0x70 bytes = 57,344 bytes"]
    SlotIdx --> ChunkBuf
    ChunkBuf --> Identity["CEntityIdentity (0x70 bytes)\n+0x00: m_pEntity (CEntityInstance*)\n+0x10: m_handle (Serial Verification)"]
    Identity --> Validate{"identity->m_handle == handle?"}
    Validate -->|Match| Instance["CEntityInstance* (C_CSPlayerPawn, etc.)"]
    Validate -->|Mismatch| Null["nullptr (Entity Stale / Desynced)"]
```

### 3.2 `CEntityIdentity` Structure (`0x70` Bytes)
Disassembled from `client.dll + 0x15d1be` (`imul rax, rdx, 0x70`):
```cpp
class CEntityIdentity {
public:
    CEntityInstance*  m_pEntity;              // +0x00: Instantiated entity object
    void*             m_pClassInfo;           // +0x08: Schema class info descriptor
    CEntityHandle     m_handle;               // +0x10: 32-bit handle (index + serial)
    std::int32_t      m_nameStringTableIndex; // +0x14: String table index
    const char*       m_pszName;              // +0x18: Entity target name
    const char*       m_pszDesignerName;      // +0x20: Designer classname ("cs_player_controller")
    std::uint64_t     m_pad28;                // +0x28: Flags / alignment
    std::uint32_t     m_flags;                // +0x30: Entity state flags
    std::uint32_t     m_pad34;                // +0x34: Alignment padding
    std::uint32_t     m_worldGroupId;         // +0x38: World partition ID
    std::uint32_t     m_fDataObjectTypes;     // +0x3C: Data object bitmask
    std::uint64_t     m_PathIndex;            // +0x40: Hierarchy path index
    void*             m_pAttributes;          // +0x48: Dynamic attribute storage
    CEntityIdentity*  m_pPrev;                // +0x50: Linked list prev
    CEntityIdentity*  m_pNext;                // +0x58: Linked list next
    CEntityIdentity*  m_pPrevByClass;         // +0x60: Next with matching class
    CEntityIdentity*  m_pNextByClass;         // +0x68: Prev with matching class
};
static_assert(sizeof(CEntityIdentity) == 0x70);
```

## 5. Phase 2: Camera, Models, Rendering & Materials (`sdk/render_scene_material.hpp`)

### 5.1 4x4 View-Projection Matrix (`VMatrix`) & World-to-Screen
- **Global ViewMatrix Array**: `client.dll + 0x256cfe0` (VA: `0x18256cfe0`)
- **Engine ViewMatrix Helper**: Disassembled at `client.dll + 0xc14fb0`:
  ```asm
  movsxd rax, ecx           ; ecx = view index (0 = local player view)
  lea rcx, [rip + 0x1958026]; 0x18256cfe0 (&g_pViewMatrix[0])
  shl rax, 6                ; rax = index * 64 bytes (sizeof(VMatrix))
  add rax, rcx              ; rax = &g_pViewMatrix[index]
  ret
  ```
- **World-to-Screen Transformation & Frustum Culling**:
  $$x_c = M_{0,0}x + M_{0,1}y + M_{0,2}z + M_{0,3}$$
  $$y_c = M_{1,0}x + M_{1,1}y + M_{1,2}z + M_{1,3}$$
  $$w_c = M_{3,0}x + M_{3,1}y + M_{3,2}z + M_{3,3}$$
  If $w_c < 0.001$, the target coordinate is behind the camera near plane and rejected.
  $$\text{Screen}_X = \frac{W}{2} \cdot \left(1.0 + \frac{x_c}{w_c}\right), \quad \text{Screen}_Y = \frac{H}{2} \cdot \left(1.0 - \frac{y_c}{w_c}\right)$$

### 5.2 `CViewRender` Frame Lifecycle
- **VTable Location**: `client.dll + 0x1c7f128` (VA: `0x181c7f128`)
- **Allocation Footprint**: `0x1D60` bytes (7,520 bytes, allocated via `g_pMemAlloc->Alloc(0x1d60)` at `client.dll + 0xc05d0f`).
- **Internal Matrix Buffer**: Stored at offset `+0x1340`.

### 6.1 `CCSGOInput` Subsystem & Singleton Lifecycle

  - `m_nSubtickMoveStepCount`: `+0x284` (number of hardware/motion input slices recorded in current frame)

- **Circular Command Buffer Hierarchy**:

$$\text{Fractional Sub-tick Interpolation}: \quad w = \text{clamp}\left(\frac{T_{\text{event}} - T_{\text{tick\_start}}}{\Delta t_{\text{tick}}}, 0.0, 1.0\right)$$
Where $\Delta t_{\text{tick}} = \frac{1}{64.0\text{ s}} = 0.015625\text{ s}$ ($15.625\text{ ms}$).

### 7.3 Volumetric Smoke Optical Occlusion (`LineOfSightThroughSmoke`)
- **Prologue Signature**: `48 8B C4 55 53 56 41 55 41 57 48 8D 68 A8 48 81 EC 30 01 00 00`
- **Current RVA (`client.dll`)**: `0x007ce470` (VA: `0x1807ce470`, baseline `0x007cd4d0`, shift `+0xfa0`).
- **Algorithm**:
  Traverses active smoke entities at `client.dll + 0x24c45b0`, steps through 32x32x32 Morton Z-order voxel bitmasks, and evaluates optical line-of-sight against authoritative `0.20f` density threshold:
  $$\text{Occlusion} = \min\left(1.0, \frac{\rho_{\text{accum}}}{0.20}\right)$$

# Chapter 21: Panorama UI Architecture, Resource Decompilation & Demo Overlays

## Executive Overview

Counter-Strike 2 utilizes Valve's **Panorama UI Engine**, an integrated GPU-accelerated framework combining declarative XML, flexbox-driven CSS3 styling, and a Google V8 JavaScript runtime embedded within `panorama.dll` and `client.dll`.

## 1. Engine Subsystems & Decompiled Pipeline

In Counter-Strike 2, all HUD panels, match draft interfaces, scoreboard cards, and the demo playback timeline are governed by Panorama.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    VPK["pak01_dir.vpk Archive"] -->|Extraction| VRF["ValveResourceFormat Decompiler"]
    VRF --> VXML["vxml_c (Compiled XML AST)"]
    VRF --> VCSS["vcss_c (Serialized CSS Rules)"]
    VRF --> VJS["vjs_c (Bytecode & String Tables)"]

    VXML -->|Decompiled| DecXML["Readable XML DOM Hierarchy"]
    VCSS -->|Decompiled| DecCSS["Clean CSS3 Flexbox Styles"]
    VJS -->|Decompiled| DecJS["Readable JavaScript Logic"]

    DecXML --> PAN["panorama.dll Runtime"]
    DecCSS --> PAN
    DecJS --> V8["Embedded Google V8 Engine"]
    V8 <--> CLI["client.dll C++ Bindings"]
```

### Key Assets Tracked in SteamTracking

## 2. ValveResourceFormat (VRF) Binary Structure

All production Source 2 assets are compiled into binary containers bearing the `_c` extension (e.g. `demo_viewer.vxml_c`).

### 16-Byte Container Header
```cpp
struct ResourceHeader_t {
    uint32_t m_nFileSize;       // Total file byte size
    uint16_t m_nHeaderVersion;  // Source 2 format version (0x000C)
    uint16_t m_nVersion;        // Resource payload version (0x0001)
    uint32_t m_nBlockOffset;    // Relative offset to block directory (0x10)
    uint32_t m_nBlockCount;     // Number of binary payload blocks
};
```

### Binary Blocks
- **`DATA`**: Primary payload containing the compiled KeyValues3 (KV3) AST tree or bytecode.
- **`REDI` (Resource Edit Info)**: Dependency graph tracking source asset paths and compile flags.
- **`NTRO`**: Structural schema introspection tables for untyped engine structs.
