## Document: 22_engine_clockdrift_and_packetentities_merge.md
# Engine Clock Drift Synchronization & Pre-Decode Packet Entities Coalescer

## 1. Executive Subsystem Summary

In recent Counter-Strike 2 engine revisions (including Build `2026-11-11_26598758`), Valve significantly overhauled two core client networking execution paths in `engine2.dll`:
1. **Sub-Tick Clock Drift Compensation & Authoritative Slamming (`CNetworkGameClient::ApplyClockDrift`)**:
   Located at virtual method slot 73 (`0x180067AA0`) of `CNetworkGameClient`, this routine regulates the relationship between client host ticks (`m_nClientTick` at offset `+0x39c`) and authoritative server packet ticks (`m_nServerTick` at offset `+0x398`). It evaluates network latency jitter margins against the maximum allowable clock drift window configured by `cl_clockdrift_max_secs`.
2. **Pre-Decode Packet Entities Delta Coalescing (`cl_packetentities_merge_before_decode`)**:
   Located in `CPacketEntitiesProcessor::ProcessEntityDeltaStream` (`0x1800441A0`), this architectural enhancement replaces the legacy two-pass entity deserialization pipeline with a unified, single-pass scratch bitstream arena merger, completely eliminating redundant intermediate field deserializations and change callback dispatch overhead.

---

## 2. Clock Drift Synchronization (`CNetworkGameClient::ApplyClockDrift`)

### 2.1 Mathematical Formulation & Drift Gating

Every incoming network packet delivers an authoritative server tick index $k_{\text{server}}$ alongside the active simulation ticks window $W_{\text{sim}}$. The client engine evaluates the clock deviation $\Delta k = k_{\text{client}} - k_{\text{server}}$.

The allowable drift threshold $T_{\text{max}}$ is dynamically calculated in `engine2.dll` @ `0x180067AA0`:

$$\begin{aligned}
k_{\text{drift\_max}} &= \text{cl\_clockdrift\_max\_secs} \times 64.0 \\
k_{\text{jitter}} &= m\_flJitterMarginSecs \times 64.0 \\
T_{\text{base}} &= \lceil k_{\text{drift\_max}} + k_{\text{jitter}} \rceil \\
T_{\text{total}} &= T_{\text{base}} + W_{\text{sim}}
\end{aligned}$$

When the absolute delta $|\Delta k|$ exceeds $T_{\text{total}}$, the engine immediately aborts smooth continuous time interpolation and executes an **authoritative tick slam**:

$$\begin{aligned}
\text{if } |\Delta k| > T_{\text{total}} \implies k_{\text{target}} = (k_{\text{client}} - W_{\text{sim}}) + 1
\end{aligned}$$

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|               Authoritative Clock Drift Threshold Gating Window                   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                                   |
|  Server Tick (k_srv)             Allowable Margin (T_total)                       |
|         |                                                                         |
|         V                                                                         |
|  [======*===============================|======================================]  |
|         <--- Continuous Proportional --->  SLAM! (Snap to Server Window)          |
|              Adjustment Region                                                    |
|                                                                                   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### 2.2 Verified Disassembly & Log Specifiers

When slamming is triggered, `engine2.dll` dispatches through the tier0 logging system:

```c
// Format specifier at 0x1805CE640:
"Slamming client tick to server tick. abs( server tick %d - client tick %d = %d ) > ( cl_clockdrift_max_ticks %.1f + sim ticks %d + jitter margin %.1f = %d )\n"

// Continuous correction format specifier at 0x1805CE600:
"[s%5d c%5d t%6.3f] ApplyClockDrift correcting %d -> %d\n"
```

### 2.3 Verified Member Offsets in `CNetworkGameClient`

| Offset | Type | Member Identifier | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `+0x398` | `int32_t` | `m_nServerTick` | Authoritative server tick index from latest packet |
| `+0x39c` | `int32_t` | `m_nClientTick` | Predicted client execution tick |
| `+0x2c356c` | `int32_t` | `m_nTargetTickClamped` | Local tick floor clamping boundary |
| `+0x2caf1c` | `float` | `m_flJitterMarginSecs` | Network packet transit jitter accumulator (seconds) |
| `+0x2caf24` | `float` | `m_flAverageDriftSecs` | Exponential moving average drift filter |
| `+0x2caf2c` | `int32_t` | `m_nSlamCount` | Total tick slamming events since map load |

---

## 3. Pre-Decode Entity Packet Coalescer (`cl_packetentities_merge_before_decode`)

### 3.1 Legacy Two-Pass Deserialization vs Single-Pass Pre-Decode Merge

In legacy Source 2 network processing, entity updates required two full deserialization passes:
1. **Pass 1 (Baseline Decompression)**: Decompresses the complete baseline entity bitstream into the entity memory slot. This deserializes all baseline fields (typically 32 to 48 fields) and triggers initial client state change callbacks.
2. **Pass 2 (Wire Delta Overlay)**: Decompresses the incoming packet delta bitstream over the same entity memory slot, overwriting baseline values with modified delta fields (typically 12 to 16 fields).

This legacy model caused two major performance bottlenecks:
- Redundant CPU deserialization work for every field present in both baseline and delta.
- Multiple redundant field change callbacks fired within the exact same frame.

### 3.2 Single-Pass Pre-Decode Consolidation Architecture

When `cl_packetentities_merge_before_decode` (ConVar at `0x1807305E8`) is enabled, `CPacketEntitiesProcessor::ProcessEntityDeltaStream` (`0x1800441A0`) short-circuits the dual decode:

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                  Single-Pass Pre-Decode Consolidation Pipeline                          |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                                         |
|   1. Baseline Bitstream  (lVar6)  ---+                                                  |
|                                      |--> MergeBitStreams() (0x60)                      |
|   2. Wire Delta Packet   (0x0c)   ---+        |                                         |
|                                               V                                         |
|                                      [ Scratch Arena Buffer ] (Allocated via 0x0)       |
|                                               |                                         |
|                                               V                                         |
|                                      Single-Pass Decode() (0x38)                        |
|                                               |                                         |
|                                               V                                         |
|                                      ReleaseScratchBuffer() (0x8)                       |
|                                                                                         |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

1. **Arena Scratch Allocation**: Invokes slot `0x0` on the allocator vtable to lease a zero-copy bitstream scratch buffer from thread-local memory.
2. **Bitstream-Level Merging**: Invokes slot `0x60` (`MergeBitStreams`). The delta bits overwrite baseline bits directly within the compressed bitstream stream without deserializing intermediate C++ objects.
3. **Unified Single-Pass Deserialization**: Invokes slot `0x38` on the flattened serializer once. All final field values are unpacked into the entity memory block simultaneously with 0 redundant callbacks.
4. **Scratch Recycling**: Invokes slot `0x8` to return the scratch buffer to the thread-local allocation arena.

---

## 4. Multi-Threaded Atomic Work-Stealing Job Dispatcher

Packet entity processing across high player counts or complex maps is parallelized through `CParallelPacketEntitiesJob::Run` (`0x1800475C0`).

Worker threads dynamically dequeue `PacketEntityWorkItem` units via atomic fetch-and-add:

```x86asm
; engine2.dll @ 0x1800475CA
lock xadd   [rdi + 0x10], rbx   ; rbx = 0xb0 (176 bytes work item stride)
cmp         rax, [rdi + 0x18]   ; check bounds against total packet items
jae         loc_finish_job
```

Each work item (`0xb0` = 176 bytes) encapsulates:
- Entity handle & class descriptor index.
- Baseline bitstream pointer & delta packet bitstream pointer.
- Scratch buffer leased pointer.
- Field counts and completion telemetry flags.

---

## 5. Reconstructed Clean-Room C++20 SDK Headers

The authoritative clean-room implementations are maintained under:
- [`game/engine/clock_drift.h`](../game/engine/clock_drift.h) & [`game/engine/clock_drift.cpp`](../game/engine/clock_drift.cpp): Exact mathematical tick slamming and drift filter.
- [`game/network/packet_entities_coalescer.h`](../game/network/packet_entities_coalescer.h) & [`game/network/packet_entities_coalescer.cpp`](../game/network/packet_entities_coalescer.cpp): Pre-decode bitstream merger and parallel job work-item stride definition.
- [`sdk/include/engine/clock_drift.hpp`](../sdk/include/engine/clock_drift.hpp) & [`sdk/include/network/packet_entities_coalescer.hpp`](../sdk/include/network/packet_entities_coalescer.hpp): SDK exposed aliases for client integration.

## Document: 23_server_parallel_snapshots.md
# Chapter 23: Server Parallel Snapshot Pipeline & Asynchronous Dispatch Architecture

## 1. Executive Subsystem Summary

In Counter-Strike 2 engine revisions (including Build `2026-11-11_26598758`), Valve introduced a multi-stage, task-graph-driven asynchronous execution model to `engine2.dll` to replace the legacy single-threaded, synchronous per-client snapshot broadcast pipeline.

Governed by internal engine ConVars (`sv_parallel_sendsnapshot`, `sv_frame_snapshot_sort_entities`, and `sv_frame_snapshot_async_delete`), this architecture transitions server delta generation into an asynchronous pipeline:
1. **Parallel Entity Packing (`CNetworkGameServer::PackEntities_Normal`)**: Shards entity baseline and delta compression across worker threads using `IThreadPool::ParallelFor`.
2. **Chunked 2D Snapshot Matrix & Tree Sorting (`CFrameSnapshotManager::CreateFrameSnapshot`)**: Organizes active entity states into a 2D chunked matrix (1024 entities per block, 32-byte descriptor). When `sv_frame_snapshot_sort_entities` is enabled, entity indices are ordered via in-order traversal of a balanced Red-Black tree (`CUtlRBTree`).
3. **Atomic Task-Graph Barrier Chaining (`CServerSideClient::SetupParallelSnapshotDependencies`)**: Under Mode 4, regular client transmission jobs form a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) with an atomic dependency counter (`m_nPendingPredecessors`). When all client snapshot jobs complete, the predecessor count drops to zero, unblocking the dependent HLTV broadcast encoder job.
4. **Deferred Asynchronous Snapshot Reclamation (`CFrameSnapshot::ReleaseReference`)**: Uses atomic reference counting (`lock xadd`). When a snapshot is released, its deletion is offloaded to the thread pool as a low-priority `CLambdaJob` to avoid tick stalls.

---

## 2. ConVar Analysis & Value Semantics

### 2.1 `sv_parallel_sendsnapshot`
- **Registration Site**: `0x1800062b0` - `0x180006357`
- **String Identifier**: `"sv_parallel_sendsnapshot"` (`0x1805d73d0`)
- **Storage Pointer**: `0x180730b58` (`m_nValue` at `+0x58` as `int32_t`)
- **Flags**: `0x80000` (`FCVAR_RELEASE`)

#### Execution Modes:
| Value | Mode Identifier | Profile & Synchronization |
|:---:|:---|:---|
| **0** | `SERIAL_SYNCHRONOUS` | Synchronous execution on main server thread. |
| **1** | `ASYNC_CLIENT_ONLY` | Asynchronous worker jobs on listen server; synchronous on dedicated server. |
| **2** | `ASYNC_UNCONDITIONAL` | Asynchronous jobs across all configurations. |
| **3** | `PARALLEL_TICK_BLOCKED` | Parallel dispatch across threads, blocking at end-of-tick barrier. |
| **4** | `PARALLEL_DAG_CHAINED` | Main server player jobs run in parallel; HLTV jobs execute once client DAG unblocks. |

### 2.2 `sv_frame_snapshot_sort_entities` & `sv_frame_snapshot_async_delete`
- **`sv_frame_snapshot_sort_entities`** (`0x18096f530`, default `1`): When enabled, `CFrameSnapshotManager::CreateFrameSnapshot` performs an in-order walk of a `CUtlRBTree` to order entity indices sequentially, improving CPU L1 cache locality during delta compression.
- **`sv_frame_snapshot_async_delete`** (`0x18096f540`, default `0`): When reference count hits zero (`lock xadd [rcx + 0xb4], -1`), wraps `CFrameSnapshotManager::DeleteFrameSnapshotInternal` into a 96-byte `CLambdaJob` (`0x1805e1718`) at `PRIORITY_LOW` on the worker pool.

---

## 3. Disassembly & Task Graph Synchronization

### 3.1 Task Graph DAG Dependency Chaining (`0x1800beb00`)
```x86asm
; engine2.dll @ 0x1800beb66
mov     rax, cs:sv_parallel_sendsnapshot_ptr
mov     eax, [rax + 0x58]
cmp     eax, 4                           ; Check for Mode 4 (DAG Chained)
jl      short loc_skip_chaining

; Atomically increment HLTV job dependency count
lock inc dword ptr [rdi + 0x88]           ; m_nPendingPredecessors atomic increment
```

### 3.2 Snapshot Send Job Class Hierarchy

|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| `CServerSideClient::CSendJob_Regular` | `0x180637cc8` | `0x1805dcd88` | `0x1800b8e30` |
| `CServerSideClient::CSendJob_Empty` | `0x180637c28` | `0x1805dc878` | `0x1800beeb0` |
| `CServerSideClient::CSendJob_HltvSource` | `0x180637bd8` | `0x1805dca58` | `0x1800bef60` |
| `CServerSideClient::CSendJob_HltvReplay` | `0x180637b88` | `0x1805dcaa8` | `0x1800bf080` |

## Document: 24_gpu_driven_occlusion_culling.md
# Chapter 24: GPU-Driven Occlusion Culling & Indirect Draw Architecture

## 1. Executive Subsystem Summary

In Counter-Strike 2 (`client.dll` & `rendersystemdx11.dll`, Build `2026-11-11_26598758`), Valve introduced a high-performance **GPU-Driven Compute Occlusion Culling & Indirect Draw Pipeline**.

Traditionally, Source 2 evaluated visibility on the CPU using PVS clusters or CPU frustum bounding-box intersections. The GPU culling architecture moves instance visibility testing entirely to compute shaders on the GPU:
1. **Depth Pyramid / Hierarchical Z-Buffer (HZB) Construction (`CDepthPyramidComputeRenderer::RenderMultiPass`)**: The depth buffer from the depth prepass is iteratively downsampled into a mip chain texture (`depthpyramid.vtex`) using `materials/dev/downsample_depth_cs.vmat`.
2. **Compute Culling Shader Dispatch (`CRenderingPipelineCsgo::AddGpuCullingLayer`)**: Reads a `StructuredBuffer<MeshCullingInstance_t>`, projects instance bounding boxes into clip space, selects the appropriate HZB mip level, and tests depth occlusion against the 4-texel quad.
3. **Indirect Argument Generation**: Surviving instances have their draw parameters written directly into a GPU buffer (`RWByteAddressBuffer`) configured with `RENDER_BUFFER_UAV_DRAW_INDIRECT_ARGS` (`0x100`).
4. **Hardware Execution (`CRenderContextDx11::DrawIndexedInstancedIndirect`)**: Dispatches `ID3D11DeviceContext::DrawIndexedInstancedIndirect` (vtable slot 39 at `0x18001C760`), executing draw calls with zero CPU readback.

---

## 2. ConVar Analysis & Value Semantics

| ConVar Name | Registration VA | ConVar Object VA | Flags | Default | Category / Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `r_csgo_gpu_culling` | `0x180123F6A` | `0x1825E4DB0` | `0x100000` (Render Thread) | `true` (1) | Main switch for GPU compute culling |
| `r_csgo_gpu_culling_camera_offset` | `0x180123FC0` | `0x1825E4DD0` | `0x2` (Hidden/Dev) | `0.0f` | Camera depth bias offset in world units |
| `r_csgo_gpu_culling_shadows` | `0x180124060` | `0x1825E4DE0` | `0x100000` (Render Thread) | `false` (0) | GPU culling for Cascaded Shadow Maps |
| `r_csgo_gpu_culling_shadows_min_cascade` | `0x180124110` | `0x1825E5190` | `0x2` (Hidden/Dev) | `1` | Minimum CSM cascade index to cull |
| `r_csgo_gpu_culling_two_pass` | `0x1801241C0` | `0x1825E4DC0` | `0x100000` (Render Thread) | `false` (0) | Two-pass occlusion culling (re-cull after prepass) |

---

## 3. Mathematical & Projection Formulas

### 3.1 Conservative Clip-Space Extent Projection
To prevent false-positive culling near screen edges or silhouette silhouettes, Valve projects the AABB extents using the absolute value matrix:
$$\text{Extent}_{\text{clip}} = \text{Extent}_x \cdot |\mathbf{M}_{0}| + \text{Extent}_y \cdot |\mathbf{M}_{1}| + \text{Extent}_z \cdot |\mathbf{M}_{2}|$$

### 3.2 HZB Mip Level Selection
Given screen-space bounding rectangle $[x_{\min}, y_{\min}, x_{\max}, y_{\max}]$ with dimensions $\Delta x, \Delta y$:
$$\text{mip} = \text{clamp}\left(\left\lceil \log_2 \left(\max(\Delta x \cdot W, \Delta y \cdot H)\right) \right\rceil, 0, \text{nMipCount} - 1\right)$$

An instance is culled if the minimum projected depth $Z_{\min}$ is behind all 4 texels of the conservative HZB mip:
$$\text{if } Z_{\min} > Z_{\text{HZB}} \implies \text{Culled (InstanceCount} = 0\text{)}$$

## 3. CEntitySystem Partitioned Chunk Array & Handle Dereference

In Source 2, entities are indexed through a 32-bit `CEntityHandle`:
$$\text{Entity Index} = \text{Handle} \ \& \ \text{0x7FFF} \quad (15\text{ bits, up to } 32,768 \text{ entities})$$
$$\text{Serial Number} = \text{Handle} \gg 15 \quad (17\text{ bits, ABA prevention})$$

The `CEntitySystem` stores entities in 64 chunks of 512 entries each:
$$\text{Chunk Index} = \text{Index} \gg 9, \quad \text{Slot Index} = \text{Index} \ \& \ \text{0x1FF}$$
$$\text{Descriptor Address} = \text{ChunkPointer} + \text{SlotIndex} \times 0\text{x}70 \quad (\text{sizeof}(CEntityIdentity) = 112\text{ bytes})$$

---

## 4. CCSPlayerController $\leftrightarrow$ CCSPlayerPawn Linkage

- **`CCSPlayerController`** (`0xAB8` bytes): Primary VFTable at `0x18190DED8`. Holds session identity, name, money, and spectator state.
  - `m_hPlayerPawn`: Offset **`+0x08EC`** (`CHandle<CCSPlayerPawn>`)
  - `m_hObserverPawn`: Offset **`+0x08F0`** (`CHandle<CBaseEntity>`)
  - `m_bPawnIsAlive`: Offset **`+0x08FC`** (`bool`)
  - `m_sSanitizedPlayerName`: Offset **`+0x051C`** (`char[128]`)
- **`CCSPlayerPawn`** (`0x15C0` bytes): Primary VFTable at `0x1817843E8`. Holds combat physical state, services, and inventory.
  - `m_hController`: Offset **`+0x0C98`** (`CHandle<CCSPlayerController>`)
  - `m_pWeaponServices`: Offset **`+0x0B10`**
  - `m_pItemServices`: Offset **`+0x0B18`**
  - `m_pMovementServices`: Offset **`+0x0B50`**
  - `m_pCameraServices`: Offset **`+0x0B48`**

### 4.1 Decompiled Handle Dereference (`0x180212390`)
```x86asm
; CCSPlayerController::GetPlayerPawn
mov     edx, dword ptr [rcx + 8ECh]    ; Load m_hPlayerPawn
cmp     edx, -1                        ; Invalid handle check
je      ret_null
mov     rcx, qword ptr [g_pEntitySystem]
and     eax, 7FFFh                     ; Index = handle & 0x7FFF
shr     rax, 9                         ; Chunk = Index / 512
mov     r9, qword ptr [rcx + rax*8]    ; Chunk pointer
and     r8d, 1FFh                      ; Slot = Index % 512
imul    rax, r8, 70h                   ; Offset = Slot * 112
add     rax, r9                        ; pIdentity
cmp     dword ptr [rax + 10h], edx     ; Verify serial number matches handle
cmovne  rax, r10                       ; If mismatch, return nullptr
mov     rax, qword ptr [rax]           ; return pIdentity->m_pEntityInstance
ret
```

# Counter-Strike 2 (Source 2) - Ballistic Penetration & Multi-Surface Material Physics Architecture (`server.dll`)

## 1. Architectural Overview: Authoritative Raycast Ballistics & Multi-Interval Physics

In Source 2 (`server.dll`), all high-velocity directional raycast queries, trajectory segment partitioning, physical surface absorption, and player pawn armor mitigation are evaluated authoritatively on the server. The client predicts muzzle flash visuals and local tracer effects, but trajectory intersection, multi-surface wallbang penetration, kinetic energy attenuation, and damage state modifications are strictly computed within the physics execution pipeline.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph BallisticsPipeline ["Source 2 Authoritative Ballistics & Multi-Surface Physics Pipeline"]
        A["Raycast Initialization (Directional Ray Vector)"] --> B["CGamePhysicsQueryInterface::TraceLineIntervals"]
        B --> C{"Interval Classifier (flags & 1)"}
        C -->|flags & 1 == 0: Air Interval| D["Evaluate Air Attenuation ODE pow(R, dist/500)"]
        C -->|flags & 1 == 1: Solid Material| E["EvaluateBulletPenetration (0x180a90280)"]
        E --> F["Rubikon Surface Descriptor Resolution (vphysics2.dll)"]
        F --> G{"Material & Distance Filter"}
        G -->|dist > 3000u OR penMod < 0.1| H["Dissipation Limit Reached (count = 0)"]
        G -->|penCount >= 1| I["Evaluate Kinetic Energy Dissipation ODE"]
        I --> J{"Remaining Energy >= 1.0?"}
        J -->|No| K["Trajectory Terminated (stopped = true)"]
        J -->|Yes| L["penCount-- & Proceed to Next Interval"]
        L --> M{"Pawn Capsule Hit?"}
        M -->|Yes| N["CCSPlayerPawn::ApplyArmorDamageCalculation (0x180a81610)"]
        N --> O["CCSPlayerPawn::IsArmored Jump Table (0x180acaca0)"]
        O --> P["Apply Durability Damping & Vitality Update"]
    end
```

---

## 2. Mathematical Formulations & Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs)

### 2.1 Atmospheric / Air Attenuation Distance Falloff
When a directional raycast traverses an unoccluded spatial interval (air interval where `flags & 1 == 0`), the projectile experiences exponential velocity and kinetic energy decay modeled by the discrete differential attenuation function:

$$\frac{dE}{dx} = -\left(\frac{\ln(\text{RangeModifier})}{500.0}\right) E(x)$$

Solving this first-order ODE over interval travel distance $\Delta d = d_{\text{exit}} - d_{\text{enter}}$ yields the authoritative closed-form energy equation executed in `server.dll` @ `0x180a902ea`:

$$E_{\text{exit}} = E_{\text{current}} \times (\text{RangeModifier})^{\frac{\Delta d}{500.0f}}$$

Where:
- $\Delta d = \max(t_{\text{exit}} \times \text{maxRange}, t_{\text{enter}} \times \text{maxRange}) - \max(0.0f, t_{\text{enter}} \times \text{maxRange})$
- $\text{RangeModifier} \in (0.0, 1.0]$: Dimensionless distance decay scalar per 500 game units (e.g., $0.98$ for AK-47, $0.99$ for AWP, $0.85$ for Desert Eagle).

### 2.2 Solid Physical Material Damping ODE
When traversing a solid physical medium (`flags & 1 == 1`), the kinetic energy loss combines distance-dependent volumetric friction and entry/exit acoustic shock dispersion:

$$\Delta E_{\text{total}} = \Delta E_{\text{distance}} + \Delta E_{\text{shock}}$$

#### 2.2.1 Volumetric Medium Damping
The energy dissipated across slab thickness $h = \|\mathbf{p}_{\text{exit}} - \mathbf{p}_{\text{enter}}\|$ scales quadratically with depth, inversely proportional to the material penetration modifier $\eta_{\text{pen}}$:

$$\eta_{\text{inv}} = \max\left(0.0f, \frac{1.0f}{\eta_{\text{pen}}}\right)$$

$$\Delta E_{\text{distance}} = \frac{h^2 \times \eta_{\text{inv}}}{24.0f}$$

Where $24.0f$ is the global volumetric damping constant loaded from `0x1817af650`.

#### 2.2.2 Shock Impedance & Material Transition Damping
Surface boundary entry triggers an immediate impedance mismatch shock loss:

$$\kappa_{\text{power}} = \max\left(0.0f, \frac{3.0f}{P_{\text{weapon}}} \times 1.25f\right)$$

$$\Delta E_{\text{shock}} = \left[\kappa_{\text{power}} \times (\eta_{\text{inv}} \times 3.0f)\right] + (\mu_{\text{damage}} \times E_{\text{current}})$$

Where:
- $P_{\text{weapon}}$: Projectile penetration power multiplier (e.g., $2.0f$ for rifles, $2.5f$ for sniper platforms).
- $1.25f$: Ballistic shock scalar constant loaded from `0x1817b9050`.
- $\mu_{\text{damage}}$: Surface shock absorption coefficient (default $0.16f$ for composite transitions).
- $3.0f$: Standard entry loss coefficient loaded from `0x181774c28`.

#### 2.2.3 Net Kinetic State Transition
$$E_{\text{next}} = E_{\text{current}} - \Delta E_{\text{total}}$$

If $E_{\text{next}} < 1.0f$, the kinetic energy drops below the minimum threshold required to overcome material tensile resistance; the projectile is halted (`stopped = true`, returns `1`).

## 5. Disassembly Analysis: `CCSPlayerPawn::ApplyArmorDamageCalculation` (RVA `0x00a81610`)

When a projectile ray impacts an active player pawn hitbox, incoming kinetic damage is routed through `CCSPlayerPawn::ApplyArmorDamageCalculation`:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Enter ApplyArmorDamageCalculation"] --> B{"m_ArmorValue > 0 AND IsArmored(hitGroup)?"}
    B -->|No| C["Record 0 AP Absorbed & Exit"]
    B -->|Yes| D["Resolve Weapon Armor Ratio: flArmorRatio = ratio * 0.5f"]
    D --> E["flNewDamage = incomingDamage * flArmorRatio"]
    E --> F["flArmorDamage = (incomingDamage - flNewDamage) * flArmorBonus"]
    F --> G{"flArmorDamage > m_ArmorValue?"}
    G -->|Yes: Exhaustion Overflow| H["flNewDamage = incoming - (m_ArmorValue / flArmorBonus)<br>flArmorDamage = m_ArmorValue<br>m_ArmorValue = 0"]
    G -->|No: Sufficient Durability| I["m_ArmorValue -= (int)flArmorDamage"]
    H --> J["Update m_flDamage on CTakeDamageInfo & Mark State Changed"]
    I --> J
```

### 5.1 Exact Assembly Implementation
```x86asm
180a81678: MOV     ESI, dword ptr [R15]          ; ESI = m_ArmorValue (at pawn + 0x1514)
180a81684: TEST    ESI, ESI                      ; Armor durability == 0?
180a81686: JZ      0x180a818ec                   ; Bypass armor if 0
180a8168e: MOV     RCX, R14                      ; RCX = this pawn
180a81691: CALL    CCSPlayerPawn_IsArmored       ; Check hitgroup coverage
180a81696: TEST    AL, AL
180a81698: JZ      0x180a818ec                   ; Bypass armor if hitgroup unarmored
180a816a7: MOVSS   XMM6, dword ptr [0x18177042c] ; XMM6 = 0.5f (flArmorRatio scale)
180a816ba: MOVAPS  XMM9, XMM6                    ; XMM9 = 0.5f (flArmorBonusMultiplier)

; Weapon Armor Ratio Extraction
180a817af: MOVSS   XMM0, dword ptr [RAX + 0x828] ; XMM0 = weaponArmorPenetrationRatio
180a817b7: MULSS   XMM0, XMM6                    ; XMM0 = ratio * 0.5f
180a817bb: MOVAPS  XMM6, XMM0                    ; XMM6 = flArmorRatio
180a817c2: MOVSS   XMM3, dword ptr [RBX + 0x44]  ; XMM3 = flIncomingDamage
180a817ca: MULSS   XMM1, XMM6                    ; XMM1 = flNewDamage = flIncomingDamage * flArmorRatio

; Armor Durability Cost
180a817e5: MOVD    XMM2, ESI                     ; XMM2 = m_ArmorValue
180a817e9: SUBSS   XMM6, XMM1                    ; XMM6 = flIncomingDamage - flNewDamage
180a817f0: CVTDQ2PS XMM2, XMM2                   ; Float conversion of m_ArmorValue
180a817f3: MULSS   XMM6, XMM9                    ; XMM6 = (diff) * flArmorBonusMultiplier
180a817fc: COMISS  XMM6, XMM2                    ; Compare flArmorDamage with m_ArmorValue
180a817ff: JBE     0x180a81817                   ; Jump if armor has sufficient durability

; Exhaustion Overflow Branch
180a81801: MOVAPS  XMM0, XMM2                    ; XMM0 = m_ArmorValue float
180a81807: DIVSS   XMM0, XMM9                    ; XMM0 = m_ArmorValue / flArmorBonus
180a8180c: XOR     ESI, ESI                      ; m_ArmorValue = 0 (fully depleted)
180a81811: SUBSS   XMM1, XMM0                    ; flNewDamage = incomingDamage - (m_ArmorValue / flArmorBonus)
180a81815: JMP     0x180a8182a

; Standard Durability Deduction Branch
180a81817: COMISS  XMM7, XMM6                    ; Compare flArmorDamage with 0.0f
180a8181a: JBE     0x180a81824
180a8181c: MOVSS   XMM6, dword ptr [0x181770430] ; Floor at 1.0f if negative
180a81824: CVTTSS2SI EAX, XMM6                   ; EAX = (int32_t)flArmorDamage
180a81828: SUB     ESI, EAX                      ; m_ArmorValue -= EAX

; Post-Mitigation State Commitment
180a81830: MOVSS   dword ptr [RBX + 0x44], XMM1  ; Commit mitigated health damage
180a81839: MOV     dword ptr [RDI + 0x4c], EAX   ; Record absorbed armor durability
180a8184f: CALL    FUN_1801b29e0                 ; NetworkStateChanged (mark dirty)
180a81854: MOV     dword ptr [R15], ESI          ; Write back m_ArmorValue
```

---

## 6. Disassembly Analysis: `CCSPlayerPawn::IsArmored` (RVA `0x00acaca0`)

The hitgroup coverage check employs an optimized 8-way indirect jump table dispatch:

```x86asm
180acaca0: XOR     R8B, R8B                      ; Return value default = false (0)
180acaca3: CMP     dword ptr [RCX + 0x1514], 0x0 ; Check m_ArmorValue <= 0
180acacaa: JLE     0x180acace8                   ; Return false
180acacac: CMP     EDX, 0x8                      ; Check hitGroup > 8
180acacaf: JA      0x180acace8                   ; Return false
180acacb1: MOVSXD  RAX, EDX                      ; RAX = (int64)hitGroup
180acacb4: LEA     R9, [0x180000000]             ; Base address
180acacbb: MOV     EDX, dword ptr [R9 + RAX*4 + 0xacacf0] ; Jump table entry RVA
180acacc3: ADD     RDX, R9                       ; Absolute target VA
180acacc6: JMP     RDX                           ; Indirect branch dispatch

; Cases 0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8: Kevlar Vest Coverage
180acacc8: MOV     R8B, 0x1                      ; Return true
180acaccb: MOVZX   EAX, R8B
180acaccf: RET

; Case 1: Head / Helmet Coverage
180acacd0: MOV     RCX, qword ptr [RCX + 0xb18]  ; RCX = m_pItemServices
180acacd7: MOV     EAX, 0x1
180acacdc: MOVZX   R8D, R8B
180acace0: CMP     byte ptr [RCX + 0x49], 0x0    ; Check m_bHasHelmet != 0
180acace4: CMOVNZ  R8D, EAX                      ; If helmet equipped, return true
180acace8: MOVZX   EAX, R8B                      ; Return false (or helmet state)
180acacec: RET
```

### 6.1 HitGroup Coverage Matrix (`0x180acacf0`)

| Index | HitGroup Identifier | Jump Table Target | Protective Equipment Evaluated | Coverage Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0` | `HITGROUP_GENERIC` | `0x180acacc8` | Kevlar Body Armor | Protected (`true`) |
| `1` | `HITGROUP_HEAD` | `0x180acacd0` | `m_pItemServices->m_bHasHelmet` (`+0x49`) | Conditional on Helmet |
| `2` | `HITGROUP_CHEST` | `0x180acacc8` | Kevlar Body Armor | Protected (`true`) |
| `3` | `HITGROUP_STOMACH` | `0x180acacc8` | Kevlar Body Armor | Protected (`true`) |
| `4` | `HITGROUP_LEFTARM` | `0x180acacc8` | Kevlar Body Armor | Protected (`true`) |
| `5` | `HITGROUP_RIGHTARM` | `0x180acacc8` | Kevlar Body Armor | Protected (`true`) |
| `6` | `HITGROUP_LEFTLEG` | `0x180acace8` | None | Unarmored (`false`) |
| `7` | `HITGROUP_RIGHTLEG` | `0x180acace8` | None | Unarmored (`false`) |
| `8` | `HITGROUP_NECK` | `0x180acacc8` | Kevlar Body Armor | Protected (`true`) |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **HitGroup 4 & 5 (Arms) Armor Protection**: In Source 2 Counter-Strike 2, projectile impacts on the player pawn's upper arms (`HITGROUP_LEFTARM` and `HITGROUP_RIGHTARM`) are routed to the Kevlar vest mitigation block and **receive full armor damage reduction**. In contrast, lower extremities (`HITGROUP_LEFTLEG` and `HITGROUP_RIGHTLEG`) always bypass armor mitigation, causing full unmitigated damage to the pawn's vitality metric.

## Document: ghidra_mcp_extensions.md
# GhidraMCP Architecture Extensions & Source 2 Analysis Toolkit

## 1. Executive Summary & Problem Statement

While standard **GhidraMCP** provides low-latency REST access to a running Ghidra instance and avoids file lock collisions (`.lock`) on Counter-Strike 2 project databases, it exhibits fundamental limitations for advanced reverse engineering:

| Architectural Gap in Standard GhidraMCP | Impact on Source 2 Reverse Engineering | Custom Toolkit Solution |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **No C++ Header / Struct Injection** | Decompiler displays raw pointer arithmetic (`*(int*)(a1 + 0x30)`) rather than struct fields. | `inject_source2_types.py` & `batch_inject_schemas.py` inject pure Source 2 vectors, handles, and complete schema classes with explicit padding into Ghidra's `DataTypeManager`. |
| **Untyped Function Signatures** | Functions default to `undefined8 FUN_180...()`, obfuscating return types, arguments, and `__fastcall` registers. | `sync_function_prototypes.py` applies authoritative C++ prototypes and calling conventions to all 46 canonical functions. |
| **No Call Graph or XRef Queries** | Finding callers, callees, or string references requires manual GUI clicks or complex scripts. | `trace_xrefs.py` performs sub-second incoming/outgoing cross-reference queries and string xref tracing via inline Java execution. |
| **Manual VTable Porting Bottlenecks** | Class hierarchies and virtual method tables must be manually located or hardcoded per build. | `scan_rtti_vtables.py` scans PE `.rdata` for MSVC x64 RTTI descriptors, discovering all polymorphic classes, VTable RVAs, and slot counts in $O(N)$ time. |
| **Fragmented Script Invocation** | Analysts must invoke multiple disjoint scripts across 11+ game modules. | `cs2_ghidra_toolkit.py` unifies status inspection, type injection, prototype synchronization, RTTI scanning, and xref tracing under a single CLI. |

---

### 3.2 Data Type & Struct Injection: `inject-types`

Populates Ghidra's `DataTypeManager` with foundational Source 2 structures and standard integer types:
- **Vectors & Angles**: `Vector2D`, `Vector`, `Vector4D`, `QAngle`, `Quaternion`, `Matrix3x4_t`, `CTransform`.
- **Entity Handles**: `CEntityIndex` (`uint32_t`), `CEntityHandle` (`uint32_t`).
- **Containers**: `CUtlStringToken`, `CUtlString`, `CUtlMemory`, `CUtlVector`.
- **Physics**: `Ray_t`, `RaycastHit_t`.
- **C99 Standard Types**: `uint8_t`, `uint16_t`, `uint32_t`, `uint64_t`, `int8_t`, `int16_t`, `int32_t`, `int64_t`.

```bash
# Inject into currently active binary
python tools/ghidra/cs2_ghidra_toolkit.py inject-types --binary vphysics2.dll

# Inject across all 11 core binaries
python tools/ghidra/cs2_ghidra_toolkit.py inject-types --all
```

### 3.3 Batch Schema Class & Struct Injection: `inject-schemas`

Parses dumped Source 2 schemas from `data/extracted_schemas/*.json` (e.g. `client.dll.json`, `server.dll.json`, `engine2.dll.json`), resolves full inheritance hierarchies (`CEntityInstance -> C_BaseEntity -> C_BaseModelEntity -> C_BasePlayerPawn -> C_CSPlayerPawn`), computes exact runtime byte offsets, and inserts explicit padding bytes (`char pad_XXXX[N];`) between non-contiguous fields.

**Problem Addressed**:
Without struct memory layouts registered in Ghidra, decompiled functions display opaque pointer arithmetic:
```c
// Before Schema Injection:
*(int *)(param_1 + 0x34c) = 100;
*(float *)(param_1 + 0x350) = 0.0f;
```
After batch injection into Ghidra's `DataTypeManager`:
```c
// After Schema Injection:
param_1->m_iHealth = 100;
param_1->m_flDamageAccumulator = 0.0f;
```

**Key Capabilities**:
1. **Linear Inheritance Flattening**: Propagates all inherited fields from root classes down to derived entities (`C_CSPlayerPawn` includes 312 unique fields spanning 14,160 bytes).
2. **Explicit Byte-Accurate Padding**: Automatically computes field gaps and emits explicit padding arrays (`char pad_0040[0x2e8];`) so `sizeof(struct)` exactly matches engine ABI.
3. **C Header Synthesis**: Generates `data/source2_generated_classes.h` containing all foundational primitives, typedefs, forward declarations, and complete struct definitions.
4. **Ghidra DataTypeManager Registration**: Uses GhidraMCP's inline Java execution bridge with Google Gson deserialization to inject pre-sized `StructureDataType` instances into `/Source2/Classes`.

**Core High-Priority Target Classes**:
- `C_BaseEntity`, `C_BaseModelEntity`, `C_CSPlayerPawn`, `CCSPlayerController`
- `CCollisionProperty`, `CPlayer_MovementServices`, `C_CSWeaponBaseGun`, `CGameSceneNode`
- `C_BasePlayerPawn`, `CEntityInstance`, `C_EconItemView`, `C_AttributeContainer`

**CLI Usage**:
```bash
# Inject core high-priority schema classes into active Ghidra program
python tools/ghidra/cs2_ghidra_toolkit.py --inject-schemas

# Target a specific binary (e.g. server.dll or client.dll)
python tools/ghidra/cs2_ghidra_toolkit.py inject-schemas --binary server.dll

# Generate C header only (without contacting Ghidra)
python tools/ghidra/cs2_ghidra_toolkit.py inject-schemas --header-only

# Inject specific classes
python tools/ghidra/cs2_ghidra_toolkit.py inject-schemas --classes C_BaseEntity,C_CSPlayerPawn,CCSPlayerController

# Inject all extracted schema classes across all modules
python tools/ghidra/cs2_ghidra_toolkit.py inject-schemas --all-classes
```

### 3.5 MSVC x64 RTTI Scanner & VTable Auto-Discovery: `scan-rtti`

Scans the `.rdata` section for MSVC 64-bit `RTTICompleteObjectLocator` descriptors:
$$\text{Signature} == 1 \quad \land \quad p\text{Self} == \text{RVA}(\text{Locator})$$

Automatically demangles the class name from `TypeDescriptor` (`.?AV<ClassName>@@`), locates the referencing VTable pointer array at $(\text{ptr} + 8)$, counts executable virtual method slots in `.text`, and labels symbols and bookmarks in Ghidra.

```bash

python tools/ghidra/cs2_ghidra_toolkit.py scan-rtti --binary vphysics2.dll

# Scan, annotate symbols/bookmarks into Ghidra, and export JSON
python tools/ghidra/scan_rtti_vtables.py --binary vphysics2.dll --annotate --export-json vphysics2_vtables.json
```

## 4. Performance & Reliability Invariants

1. **Transaction Safety**: All modifications to Ghidra's AST, `DataTypeManager`, and `SymbolTable` are wrapped in atomic transactions (`startTransaction` / `endTransaction`).
2. **Lock Independence**: Executes strictly through GhidraMCP's in-memory REST bridge, preventing SQLite and repository `.lock` contention with the Ghidra GUI.
3. **Sub-Second Latency**: Inverted index lookups in Java allow RTTI and VTable discovery across 500,000+ `.rdata` bytes in under 2 seconds per binary.
4. **Zero Binaries in Git**: All tools output structured JSON or modify the local Ghidra project database; no compiled binaries are committed.

## Document: inferno_combustion_physics.md
# Source 2 CS2 Surface Combustion & Thermal Energy Grid Architecture

## Executive Architecture Summary
In Counter-Strike 2 (Source 2 engine, `server.dll` Build 26598758), incendiary and molotov combustion dynamics are modeled via an authoritative surface-aligned thermal propagation grid entity (`CInferno` server-side, `C_Inferno` client-side). Rather than utilizing a simple volumetric sphere, Source 2 simulates combustion using a dynamic 2D/3D flame cluster network of up to 64 discrete spatial nodes (`InfernoFlameNode_t`), downward displacement ground-snapping raycasts, slope-traversal gating, mutual volumetric smoke interaction (`CSmokeVoxelGrid`), and a non-linear exposure-scaled area damage model.

This technical architecture report documents the disassembled routines, mathematical formulations, register mappings, schema data layouts, and physical interactions reverse-engineered from `server.dll`.

---

## 1. Disassembled Function Inventory (Build 26598758)

The table below catalogs the core combustion and thermal propagation routines reverse-engineered in `server.dll`:

| Function Identifier | Symbol Name | Baseline RVA | Current RVA (Build 26598758) | Current VA | Delta | Architectural Responsibility |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `server_inferno_think` | `CInferno::InfernoThink` | `0x003427b0` | `0x00346090` | `0x180346090` | `+0x38e0` | Main per-tick simulation loop: orchestrates burnout checks, smoke extinguishment, radial spreading, and damage dispatch. |
| `server_inferno_check_expired` | `CInferno::CheckExpired` | `0x0033d4c0` | `0x00340bc0` | `0x180340bc0` | `+0x38e0` | Evaluates individual node ignition lifetimes, peak burn plateaus, and transitions cluster to post-effect decay. |
| `server_inferno_spread` | `CInferno::Spread` | `0x0034b560` | `0x0034ef00` | `0x18034ef00` | `+0x39a0` | Dynamic 2D/3D surface propagation: computes surface tangents, slope limits, step heights, and ground-snapping raycasts. |
| `server_inferno_extinguish` | `CInferno::ExtinguishFire` | `0x00340eb0` | `0x00344790` | `0x180344790` | `+0x38e0` | Quenches individual flame nodes, stops sound loops, and emits steam dissipation particle events. |
| `server_inferno_extinguish_smoke` | `CInferno::ExtinguishOverlappingSmoke` | `0x00342b10` | `0x00346330` | `0x180346330` | `+0x38e0` | Iterates active flames against smoke grids; executes authoritative 1/3rd coverage threshold full-cluster extinguishment. |
| `server_inferno_damage` | `CInferno::InfernoThink (damage)` | `0x00342f90` | `0x003468c4` | `0x1803468c4` | `+0x38e0` | Evaluates player proximity (48u), radial distance falloff (24..48u), exposure ramp multiplier (1.0x to 2.5x), and armor absorption. |

## 2. Mathematical Formulation & Surface Alignment

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
|               Incendiary Detonation Event                   |
|               Initial Seed Origin: (Cx, Cy, Cz)             |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                               |
                               v
               [Downward Ground Probe Raycast]
                 Start: (Cx, Cy, Cz + 32.0 units)
                 End  : (Cx, Cy, Cz - 64.0 units)
                               |
                               +------------------------------+
                               |                              |
                               v                              v
                    [Hit Detected]                   [Miss / Abyss]
                 Snap Position: Phit + N * 2.0u       Abort Spawn
                 Store Normal : BurnNormal[0] = N
                               |
                               v
            +------------------------------------+
            | Node 0 Seed Active Combustion Grid |
            |      m_firePositions[0] = P0       |
            |      m_bFireIsBurning[0] = true    |
            |      m_fireCount = 1               |
            +------------------------------------+
                               |
                               v
            [Periodic Spread Timer Tick: Delta t = 0.08s]
                 16 Angular Candidate Rays (Delta theta = 22.5 deg)
                 Surface Tangent Vector Projection:
                   v_tan = v - (v . N_parent) * N_parent
                 Step Distance: R_step = 36.0 units
                               |
             +-----------------+-----------------+
             |                                   |
             v                                   v
   [Slope Angle Check]                 [Step Height Check]
     N_hit.z >= 0.7071 (<= 45 deg)       |Z_hit - Z_parent| <= 44.0 units
             |                                   |
             +-----------------+-----------------+
                               |
                               v
            [Spatial Proximity & Clearance Check]
              Min Distance to Active Nodes >= 24.0 units
              Distance to Cluster Origin <= 250.0 units
                               |
                               v
                 [Add Child Node: m_fireCount < 64]
```

### 2.1 Downward Ground-Snapping Raycasting
When an incendiary or molotov projectile impacts a surface, or when a child flame node is evaluated during radial expansion, the tentative 3D position $\mathbf{P}_{\text{test}} = (x, y, z)$ is snapped to uneven world geometry (including displacement brushes and uneven meshes) via an orthogonal vertical raycast:
$$\mathbf{R}_{\text{start}} = \mathbf{P}_{\text{test}} + (0, 0, \Delta z_{\text{up}}), \quad \Delta z_{\text{up}} = +32.0 \text{ units}$$
$$\mathbf{R}_{\text{end}} = \mathbf{P}_{\text{test}} - (0, 0, \Delta z_{\text{down}}), \quad \Delta z_{\text{down}} = -64.0 \text{ units}$$

If the ray intersects a brush face at distance $t \in [0, 1]$ with contact position $\mathbf{P}_{\text{hit}}$ and contact normal $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\text{hit}}$, the node position is aligned with a normal lift offset $\delta = +2.0 \text{ units}$ to eliminate visual z-fighting:
$$\mathbf{P}_{\text{node}} = \mathbf{P}_{\text{hit}} + 2.0 \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\text{hit}}$$
$$\mathbf{N}_{\text{node}} = \hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\text{hit}}$$

### 2.2 Surface Tangent Plane Projection
To propagate naturally along uneven displacements and sloped ramps, directional vectors are projected onto the tangent plane defined by the parent node's normal $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\text{parent}}$:
$$\hat{\mathbf{v}}_{\text{cand}} = (\cos\theta, \sin\theta, 0)$$
$$\mathbf{v}_{\text{tangent}} = \hat{\mathbf{v}}_{\text{cand}} - (\hat{\mathbf{v}}_{\text{cand}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\text{parent}})\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\text{parent}}$$
$$\hat{\mathbf{v}}_{\text{tangent}} = \frac{\mathbf{v}_{\text{tangent}}}{\|\mathbf{v}_{\text{tangent}}\|}$$

The tentative horizontal candidate position is projected at step distance $R_{\text{step}} = 36.0 \text{ units}$:
$$\mathbf{P}_{\text{cand}} = \mathbf{P}_{\text{parent}} + 36.0 \cdot \hat{\mathbf{v}}_{\text{tangent}}$$

### 2.3 Slope Climbing & Obstruction Gating
In `server.dll` (`CInferno::Spread` at RVA `0x0034ef00`), expansion is constrained by three physical invariants:
1. **Slope Traversal Threshold**: The surface normal of the contact surface must satisfy:
   $$n_{z, \text{hit}} \ge \cos(45^\circ) \approx 0.7071$$
   If $n_{z, \text{hit}} < 0.7071$, the surface is classified as a steep cliff, wall, or inverted overhang, and flame expansion is blocked.
2. **Step Height Threshold**: The vertical step height between parent and child node must not exceed:
   $$|\mathbf{P}_{z, \text{hit}} - \mathbf{P}_{z, \text{parent}}| \le 44.0 \text{ units}$$
3. **Minimum Spatial Clearance**: The child node must maintain a minimum distance from all existing active burning nodes to avoid over-clustering:
   $$\min_{j < N} \|\mathbf{P}_{\text{child}} - \mathbf{P}_j\| \ge 24.0 \text{ units}$$

---

## 3. Dynamic 2D/3D Surface Propagation Algorithm

### 3.1 Clustered Expansion Step
Propagation is executed in discrete hops governed by `m_NextSpreadTimer` ($\Delta t = 0.08\text{s}$, approximately 12.5 Hz). During each spread pulse:
- The engine iterates through active parent nodes.
- Samples 16 radial directions:
  $$\theta_k = \theta_0 + k \cdot \frac{2\pi}{16}, \quad k \in [0, 15]$$
  where $\theta_0$ is an angular phase offset determined by `m_nSpreadCount` to prevent directional bias.
- A maximum of 4 child nodes may be added per spread step.
- Expansion halts once `m_fireCount` reaches `MAX_INFERNO_FIRES` ($64$).
- Candidate nodes exceeding the maximum cluster radius ($R_{\max} = 250.0 \text{ units}$ from `m_vecOriginalSpawnLocation`) are pruned.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Active Parent Node (Position P, Normal N)"] --> B["Generate 16 Radial Rays (Step = 36.0u)"]
    B --> C["Project onto Surface Tangent Plane"]
    C --> D["Downcast Ground Snap Probe (+32u to -64u)"]
    D --> E{"Surface Hit?"}
    E -- No --> F["Reject Candidate"]
    E -- Yes --> G{"Normal.z >= 0.7071?"}
    G -- No: Wall / Cliff --> F
    G -- Yes --> H{"Delta Z <= 44.0u?"}
    H -- No: Too Steep --> F
    H -- Yes --> I{"Min Node Separation >= 24.0u?"}
    I -- No: Overcrowded --> F
    I -- Yes --> J{"Cluster Radius <= 250.0u?"}
    J -- No --> F
    J -- Yes --> K["Append Flame Node (m_fireCount++)"]
```

---

## 4. Flame Node Combustion Lifecycle

Each individual node in the 64-node array tracks its own ignition lifecycle, modeled via a 3-stage piecewise normalized thermal intensity function $I(t) \in [0.0, 1.0]$:

```
Thermal Intensity I(t)
 1.0 +---------------+=============================+---------------+
     |              /|                             |\              |
     |             / |                             | \             |
     |            /  |                             |  \            |
     |           /   |                             |   \           |
     |          /    |                             |    \          |
     |         /     |                             |     \         |
 0.0 +--------+------+-----------------------------+------+--------+
             t=0   t_warmup                    t_lifetime-t_fade  t_lifetime
             [Warmup: 0.35s]    [Peak Burn: 5.65s]      [Fade: 1.00s]
                               [Total Lifetime: 7.00s]
```

Mathematical formulation:
$$I(t) = \begin{cases} 
\frac{t - t_{\text{ign}}}{t_{\text{warmup}}} & 0 \le t - t_{\text{ign}} < t_{\text{warmup}} \\
1.0 & t_{\text{warmup}} \le t - t_{\text{ign}} < t_{\text{lifetime}} - t_{\text{fade}} \\
1.0 - \frac{(t - t_{\text{ign}}) - (t_{\text{lifetime}} - t_{\text{fade}})}{t_{\text{fade}}} & t_{\text{lifetime}} - t_{\text{fade}} \le t - t_{\text{ign}} < t_{\text{lifetime}} \\
0.0 & \text{otherwise (Burnout)}
\end{cases}$$

Where default engine parameters are:
- $t_{\text{warmup}} = 0.35 \text{ seconds}$
- $t_{\text{fade}} = 1.00 \text{ seconds}$
- $t_{\text{lifetime}} = 7.00 \text{ seconds}$

---

## 5. Mutual Smoke Voxel Interaction & Extinguishment

### 5.1 The Authoritative 1/3rd Extinguishment Rule
Extracted from `server.dll` RVA `0x00346330` - `0x0034645f`:
```
Molotov extinguished: when %d/%d fire areas were covered by smoke (exceeded 1/3rd).
```

When an active volumetric smoke grenade (`CSmokeGrenadeProjectile` / `CSmokeVoxelGrid`) is present within the cluster vicinity:
1. **Core Detonation Sphere Query**: Any flame node whose distance to the smoke detonation center $\mathbf{C}_{\text{smoke}}$ is $\le 144.0 \text{ units}$ is extinguished immediately:
   $$\|\mathbf{P}_{\text{node}} - \mathbf{C}_{\text{smoke}}\| \le 144.0 \implies \text{ExtinguishNode}(i)$$
2. **Morton 3D Voxel Query**: For nodes outside the 144-unit core sphere, their world position is converted into the $32 \times 32 \times 32$ Morton-dilated voxel grid:
   $$V_x = \lfloor (P_x - C_x) \times 0.05 + 16.0 \rfloor$$
   $$V_y = \lfloor (P_y - C_y) \times 0.05 + 16.0 \rfloor$$
   $$V_z = \lfloor (P_z - C_z) \times 0.05 + 16.0 \rfloor$$
   If `IsVoxelActive(Vx, Vy, Vz)` evaluates to true, the flame node is quenched.
3. **Cluster Quench Gate**:
   If the ratio of extinguished flame nodes to total allocated nodes meets or exceeds $33.333\%$ ($1/3\text{rd}$):
   $$\frac{N_{\text{extinguished}}}{N_{\text{total}}} \ge \frac{1}{3} \quad (\text{for } N_{\text{total}} \ge 3)$$
   The engine executes `CInferno::ExtinguishAll()`, immediately terminating the entire fire cluster, transitioning to `m_bInPostEffectTime = true`, and playing `Molotov.Extinguish`.

### 5.2 Detonation Inside Active Smoke
If an incendiary or molotov projectile detonates inside an active smoke volume ($\|\mathbf{P}_{\text{det}} - \mathbf{C}_{\text{smoke}}\| \le 144.0\text{u}$ or inside an active voxel):
- `m_bWasCreatedInSmoke` is set to `true`.
- Zero flame nodes are spawned (`m_fireCount = 0`).
- The entity enters immediate post-effect state (`m_bInPostEffectTime = true`) and is discarded.

---

## 6. Area Damage Model & Exposure Escalation ODE

In `server.dll` (`CInferno::InfernoThink` damage phase at RVA `0x003468c4`), damage is evaluated every 100ms ($\Delta t = 0.10\text{s}$, 10 Hz).

### 6.1 Distance to Flame Network
For any target pawn (`C_CSPlayerPawn`) at world position $\mathbf{P}_{\text{target}}$, the engine calculates the minimum 2D distance to any active, unextinguished flame node:
$$d_{\min} = \min_{i \in \text{Active}} \|\mathbf{P}_{\text{target}, xy} - \mathbf{P}_{i, xy}\|$$
subject to vertical bounds:
$$|\mathbf{P}_{\text{target}, z} - \mathbf{P}_{i, z}| \le 64.0 \text{ units}$$

### 6.2 Radial Falloff Factor
If $d_{\min} \le 48.0 \text{ units}$, the target is inside the damage field:
$$F_{\text{dist}} = \begin{cases}
1.0 & d_{\min} \le 24.0 \text{ units (Core Zone)} \\
1.0 - 0.5 \times \frac{d_{\min} - 24.0}{48.0 - 24.0} & 24.0 < d_{\min} \le 48.0 \text{ units (Falloff Zone)} \\
0.0 & d_{\min} > 48.0 \text{ units}
\end{cases}$$

### 6.3 Exposure Ramp Multiplier
As a player remains continuously inside the fire volume, exposure duration $t_{\text{exposure}}$ accumulates on `m_damageRampTimer`:
$$F_{\text{ramp}} = 1.0 + 1.5 \times \min\left(\frac{t_{\text{exposure}}}{2.0}, 1.0\right)$$
- At entry ($t=0$): $F_{\text{ramp}} = 1.0\times$ (deals $4.0$ base damage per tick $\approx 40$ HP/s).
- At peak exposure ($t \ge 2.0\text{s}$): $F_{\text{ramp}} = 2.5\times$ (deals $10.0$ raw damage per tick $\approx 100$ HP/s).

### 6.4 Armor Mitigation Model
Fire applies armor penetration at a fixed ratio of $85\%$ (`INFERNO_ARMOR_PENETRATION = 0.85`):
$$\text{Damage}_{\text{raw}} = D_{\text{base}} \times F_{\text{ramp}} \times F_{\text{dist}} \times I_{\text{thermal}}$$
$$\text{Damage}_{\text{health}} = \text{Damage}_{\text{raw}} \times 0.85$$
$$\text{Damage}_{\text{armor}}  = \text{Damage}_{\text{raw}} \times 0.15$$

---

# Counter-Strike 2 (Source 2) - KeyValues3 (KV3) & Resource Container Architecture (`resourcesystem.dll`)

> **Binary Target**: `resourcesystem.dll` (Base Address: `0x180000000`, Image Size: ~1,572,864 bytes)  
> **Subsystems Analyzed**: `CResourceSystem`, `CKV3Document`, `KV3Value`, `CResourceFile`, `ResourceHeader_t`, `CLZ4Codec`, `CZSTDCodec`  
> **Core Specifications**: KeyValues3 Text/Binary Format, Valve Compiled Resource Container (`VASU`), LZ4 Block Codec, Zstandard (ZSTD) Frame Metadata  
> **Verification Status**: 6 / 6 Test Suites Verified with MSVC x64 (`/std:c++20 /O2 /EHsc /W4 /WX`) ([`cs2_kv3_deserializer_sim.cpp`](simulators/cs2_kv3_deserializer_sim.cpp))

## 1. KeyValues3 (KV3) Architecture in Source 2

In Counter-Strike 2 and the Source 2 engine, **KeyValues3 (KV3)** serves as the universal object serialization format, replacing the legacy KeyValues (KV1) text format from Source 1. KV3 provides a strongly typed, hierarchical object-graph notation that supports both human-readable text representations and highly optimized binary streams (`VKV3`).

KeyValues3 is utilized across all Source 2 asset pipelines, including:
1. **Material System 2 (`vmat_c`)**: Shader graph definitions, blend parameters, material attributes.
2. **Model System (`vmdl_c`)**: Skeleton hierarchies, LOD groupings, bone attachments, mesh bindings.
3. **Sound System (`vsnd_c`, `vsndevts_c`)**: Acoustic sound event graphs, operator stacks, spatial audio parameters.
4. **Physics Subsystem (`vphys_c`)**: Rubikon collision hulls, surface friction parameters, joint constraints.
5. **Entity & Schema Systems**: Dynamic configuration tables, game rule overrides, navigation mesh metadata.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph ResourcePipeline ["Source 2 Resource Compilation Pipeline"]
        SourceAsset["Source Asset (.vmdl_input, .vmat, .kv3)"]
        Compiler["resourcecompiler.exe / resourcesystem.dll"]
    end

    subgraph ContainerFormat ["Compiled Resource Container ('VASU' / 0x55534156)"]
        Header["ResourceHeader_t (Magic, Version, Flags, BlockTable)"]
        RED2Block["Block: 'RED2' (External Dependency Paths)"]
        DATABlock["Block: 'DATA' (Asset Payload Stream)"]
        RERLBlock["Block: 'RERL' (External Resource List)"]
        REDIBlock["Block: 'REDI' (Compiler Edit Metadata)"]
    end

    subgraph KV3Engine ["KeyValues3 Deserialization Engine"]
        StreamDetect{"Stream Magic Detector"}
        TextParser["Text Lexer & Parser (<!-- kv3 ... -->)"]
        BinaryParser["Binary VKV3 Reader (Magic: 'VKV3')"]
        LZ4Decompress["CLZ4Codec Block Decompressor"]
        ZSTDDecompress["CZSTDCodec Frame Inspector"]
        ASTTree["Dynamic In-Memory Tree (KV3Value)"]
    end

    SourceAsset --> Compiler
    Compiler --> ContainerFormat
    Header --> RED2Block
    Header --> DATABlock
    Header --> RERLBlock
    Header --> REDIBlock

    DATABlock --> StreamDetect
    StreamDetect -->|Text Header| TextParser
    StreamDetect -->|Binary VKV3| BinaryParser
    BinaryParser -->|LZ4 Flag| LZ4Decompress
    BinaryParser -->|ZSTD Flag| ZSTDDecompress
    LZ4Decompress --> ASTTree
    ZSTDDecompress --> ASTTree
    BinaryParser -->|Uncompressed| ASTTree
    TextParser --> ASTTree
```

## 2. KeyValues3 Format Specification

### 2.1 Header Identification & GUID Signatures
Every KeyValues3 stream begins with an identification block that explicitly specifies the encoding mechanism and data format definition using 128-bit Universally Unique Identifiers (UUID / GUID):

```
<!-- kv3 encoding:text:version{e21c7f3c-8a33-41c5-9977-a76d3a32aa0d} format:generic:version{74477221-4c60-44d8-a14a-03838b558f68} -->
```

| Field Name | Canonical GUID | Subsystem Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`encoding:text`** | `{e21c7f3c-8a33-41c5-9977-a76d3a32aa0d}` | Standard UTF-8 textual representation. |
| **`encoding:binary`** | `{460127b0-8c20-4823-9156-9e166f9e66cb}` | Binary KV3 with LZ4 block compression. |
| **`encoding:binary_v3`**| `{1b81e69c-89da-4f60-8b85-a7012e339bfb}` | Modern Source 2 binary KV3 encoding. |
| **`format:generic`** | `{74477221-4c60-44d8-a14a-03838b558f68}` | Generic dynamic object schema. |
| **`format:vmat`** | `{07e60058-29e8-468a-8260-d667cbe5f272}` | Material System 2 shader configuration. |
| **`format:vmdl`** | `{a730e62d-1149-450e-b870-711e3b69288e}` | Model System skeletal and mesh data. |

### 2.2 Text KV3 Grammar & Data Types
The text representation supports C-style comments (`//` and `/* ... */`), XML comments (`<!-- ... -->`), and rich data types:

1. **Null**: `null` (evaluates to empty/unassigned variant).
2. **Boolean**: `true` or `false`.
3. **Integer**: 64-bit signed integers (e.g. `42`, `-1050`, `0x7FFF`).
4. **Double**: 64-bit IEEE-754 floating-point numbers (e.g. `3.141592`, `-0.001`, `1e-5`).
5. **String**: Quoted literal `"characters/models/tm_phoenix.vmdl"` or multiline `"""..."""` with escape sequences (`\n`, `\t`, `\\`, `\"`).
6. **Binary Blob**: Byte sequence prefixed with `#[` and closed with `]` (e.g. `#[ 56 41 53 55 01 00 0C 00 ]`).
7. **Array**: Ordered list enclosed in brackets `[ item1, item2, item3 ]`.
8. **Table / Object**: Associative map enclosed in braces `{ key1 = val1, key2 = val2 }`.

```
{
    m_sModelName = "models/weapons/v_rifle_primary.vmdl"
    m_nHitboxSets = 1
    m_flMassKg = 3.450000
    m_bIsSerialized = true
    m_pNullReference = null
    m_aBoundingExtents = [ -16.0, -8.5, 0.0, 16.0, 8.5, 32.0 ]
    m_subHierarchy = 
    {
        m_sBoneAttachment = "weapon_hand_R"
        m_nBoneIndex = 7
    }
    m_rawSignature = #[ 56 41 53 55 01 00 0C 00 ]
}
```

---

## 3. Binary KeyValues3 (`VKV3`) Wire Specification

Binary KeyValues3 delivers high throughput and instant loading without lexical parsing overhead.

### 3.1 Binary Header Structure (24 Bytes)
```
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Offset | Type     | Field Name       | Value                |
|--------+----------+------------------+----------------------|
| 0x00   | uint32   | m_nMagic         | 'VKV3' (0x33564B56)  |
| 0x04   | uint8[16]| m_formatGuid     | Format UUID          |
| 0x14   | uint32   | m_eCompression   | 0=None, 1=LZ4, 2=ZSTD|
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
```

When compression is enabled (`m_eCompression != 0`), an 8-byte compression trailer directly follows the 24-byte header:
```
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Offset | Type     | Field Name       | Description          |
|--------+----------+------------------+----------------------|
| 0x18   | uint32   | m_nUncompressed  | Uncompressed size    |
| 0x1C   | uint32   | m_nCompressed    | Compressed size      |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### 3.2 String Table & Dictionary Deduplication
Binary KV3 decouples string storage from node topology. Strings across key names and string values are consolidated into a prefixed dictionary at the start of the uncompressed stream:
- `uint32 m_nStringCount`: Total number of unique string entries.
- Sequential string records: `uint32 m_nLength` followed by UTF-8 bytes.

Nodes reference strings by their 0-based 32-bit table index, reducing memory footprint and speeding up hash token comparisons (`CUtlStringToken`).

### 3.3 Dynamic Node Serialization Layout
Each node in the binary payload begins with an 8-bit type discriminant:

| Type ID | Enum Name | Wire Representation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `0x00` | `KV3Type::Null` | 0 bytes payload. |
| `0x01` | `KV3Type::Boolean` | 1 byte (`0` = false, `1` = true). |
| `0x02` | `KV3Type::Integer` | 8 bytes signed little-endian (`int64_t`). |
| `0x03` | `KV3Type::Double` | 8 bytes IEEE-754 double (`double`). |
| `0x04` | `KV3Type::String` | 4 bytes unsigned string table index (`uint32_t`). |
| `0x05` | `KV3Type::BinaryBlob` | 4 bytes byte count $N$, followed by $N$ raw bytes. |
| `0x06` | `KV3Type::Array` | 4 bytes count $C$, followed by $C$ serialized `KV3Value` nodes. |
| `0x07` | `KV3Type::Table` | 4 bytes count $P$. Each pair: 4-byte key string index + value node. |

---

## 4. Block Compression Engine: Pure ISO C++20 Codecs

To strictly honor **Rule 4** (pure ISO C++20, zero external dependencies), self-contained codecs are implemented directly within `game/resourcesystem/kv3_parser.cpp`.

### 4.1 LZ4 Block Decompression Algorithm
The LZ4 block format processes sequences of literal bytes and backwards dictionary matches:

$$\text{Token} = (\text{Literal Length Code} \ll 4) \mid (\text{Match Length Code})$$

1. **Literal Length**: If high nibble is `15`, read successive bytes while byte equals `255`, summing into total literal count.
2. **Literal Copy**: Copy literal bytes directly from source to destination buffer.
3. **Offset Read**: Read 16-bit unsigned little-endian offset ($\Delta \in [1, 65535]$).
4. **Match Length**: If low nibble is `15`, read successive bytes while byte equals `255`, adding to base length ($\text{Length} = \text{val} + 4$).
5. **Overlapping Copy**: Copy $\text{Length}$ bytes from `dst - offset` into `dst` (handling RLE where $\text{offset} = 1$).

```cpp
bool CLZ4Codec::Decompress(std::span<const std::uint8_t> src, std::span<std::uint8_t> dst) {
    std::size_t srcPos = 0, dstPos = 0;
    while (srcPos < src.size()) {
        const std::uint8_t token = src[srcPos++];
        std::size_t literalLen = token >> 4;
        if (literalLen == 15) {
            while (srcPos < src.size()) {
                const std::uint8_t extra = src[srcPos++];
                literalLen += extra;
                if (extra != 255) break;
            }
        }
        if (srcPos + literalLen > src.size() || dstPos + literalLen > dst.size()) return false;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < literalLen; ++i) dst[dstPos++] = src[srcPos++];
        if (srcPos >= src.size()) break;
        const std::uint16_t offset = src[srcPos] | (src[srcPos + 1] << 8);
        srcPos += 2;
        if (offset == 0 || offset > dstPos) return false;
        std::size_t matchLen = (token & 0x0F) + 4;
        if ((token & 0x0F) == 15) {
            while (srcPos < src.size()) {
                const std::uint8_t extra = src[srcPos++];
                matchLen += extra;
                if (extra != 255) break;
            }
        }
        if (dstPos + matchLen > dst.size()) return false;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < matchLen; ++i) {
            dst[dstPos] = dst[dstPos - offset];
            dstPos++;
        }
    }
    return dstPos == dst.size();
}
```

### 4.2 ZSTD Frame Inspection & Raw Block Decoding
Source 2 updates increasingly utilize Zstandard compression for large asset streams. `CZSTDCodec` inspects the Zstandard frame header (`0xFD2FB528`), extracts single-segment and content size flags from the Frame Header Descriptor (FHD), and decodes uncompressed blocks across block boundaries.

---

## 5. Source 2 Compiled Resource Container (`ResourceHeader_t`)

Source 2 compiled asset files (e.g., `*.vmdl_c`, `*.vmat_c`, `*.vsnd_c`, `*.vphys_c`) wrap payloads in a standardized container format.

### 5.1 Container Binary Layout
```
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Offset | Type     | Field Name       | Description                      |
|--------+----------+------------------+----------------------------------|
| 0x00   | uint32   | m_nMagic         | 0x55534156 ("VASU" Little-Endian)|
| 0x04   | uint16   | m_nHeaderVersion | Typically 12 (0x000C)            |
| 0x06   | uint16   | m_nVersion       | Compilation asset version        |
| 0x08   | uint32   | m_nFlags         | Compiler & endian flags          |
| 0x0C   | uint32   | m_nBlockOffset   | Offset to block descriptor table |
| 0x10   | uint32   | m_nBlockCount    | Total number of resource blocks  |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### 5.2 Resource Block Descriptor (`ResourceBlockEntry_t`)
Each block entry in the table occupies 12 bytes:
```
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Offset | Type     | Field Name       | Description                      |
|--------+----------+------------------+----------------------------------|
| 0x00   | uint32   | m_nBlockId       | FourCC ('DATA', 'RED2', 'RERL')  |
| 0x04   | uint32   | m_nOffset        | Absolute byte offset in file     |
| 0x08   | uint32   | m_nSize          | Uncompressed byte length         |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### 5.3 Canonical Block FourCC Identifiers
- **`DATA` (`0x41544144`)**: Compiled asset data. In modern Source 2, this block contains an embedded binary `VKV3` stream or specialized engine buffers.
- **`RED2` (`0x32444552`)**: External Resource References (v2). Stores a list of referenced file paths (materials, models, sounds, physics hulls) and their 64-bit content hashes.
- **`RERL` (`0x4C524552`)**: Legacy Resource External Reference List (v1).
- **`REDI` (`0x49444552`)**: Resource Edit Information (compiler version, compile arguments, source file timestamps).
- **`VBIB` (`0x42494256`)**: Vertex Buffer and Index Buffer mesh primitives.
- **`NTRO` (`0x4F52544E`)**: Introspection Schema metadata table.

---

## 6. Implementation Architecture (`game/resourcesystem/`)

The reconstructed serialization engine is modularized across:
- **`game/resourcesystem/kv3_parser.h`**: Type definitions, `KV3Value` variant container, GUID helpers, `CKV3Document`, `CResourceFile`, codec classes.
- **`game/resourcesystem/kv3_parser.cpp`**: Lexer, recursive descent parser, text formatter, binary VKV3 serializer/deserializer, LZ4 codec, container builder.

### 6.1 `KV3Value` Dynamic Variant Architecture
`KV3Value` encapsulates a `std::variant` over 8 distinct types:
```cpp
using Storage = std::variant<
    std::monostate, // Null
    bool,           // Boolean
    std::int64_t,   // Integer
    double,         // Double
    std::string,    // String
    KV3Blob,        // Binary Blob (std::vector<uint8_t>)
    KV3Array,       // Array (std::vector<KV3Value>)
    KV3Table        // Table / Object (std::vector<std::pair<std::string, KV3Value>>)
>;
```
Key accessor features:
- **Null Safety**: Accessing missing table keys or array indices returns a null sentinel without throwing exceptions or causing memory corruption.
- **Type Coercion**: `AsInt()`, `AsDouble()`, `AsString()`, `AsBool()` provide safe fallbacks with user-supplied default values.
- **Deep Traversal**: Fluent chaining syntax `doc.Root()["player"]["inventory"][1].AsString()`.

## Document: lag_compensation_rollback.md
# Source 2 CS2 Authoritative Temporal Rollback & Lag Compensation (`server.dll`)

## Executive Architectural Summary
In Counter-Strike 2 (Source 2 engine, `server.dll` Build 26598758), spatial query authoritativeness and kinematic synchronization are executed server-side through the **Authoritative Temporal History Rollback and Lag Compensation System** (`CLagCompensationManager`). 

Because network transport latency causes remote client viewports to render entity positions at historic timestamps, client commands operate on delayed visual coordinates. To resolve directional spatial raycasts (e.g. line-of-sight and ballistic trajectories) without client-side authoritativeness, `server.dll` maintains a continuous, per-entity temporal ring buffer of past transformation states. Upon receiving a sub-tick timestamped command packet, the server temporarily rewinds all target entity spatial volume bounds and skeletal bone matrices to the continuous time instant perceived by the client, executes ray-box geometric intersection tests, and authoritatively restores each entity to its present simulation frame with 100% bit-exact precision.

---

## 2. Temporal Ring Buffer Architecture & Memory Layout

```mermaid

    end

    ManagerState --> TrackedPawn
```
